title.zh: 卷240 列傳二十七 李国英 刘武元 库礼 胡全才 申朝纪 于时跃 吴景道 刘清泰 陈锦
title.en: Volume 240 Biographies 27: Li Guoying, Liu Wuyuan, Ku Li, Hu Quancai, Shen Chaoji, Yu Shiyue, Wu Jingdao, Liu Qingtai, Chen Jin
title.raw: 卷240 列傳二十七 李国英 刘武元 库礼 胡全才 申朝纪 于时跃 吴景道 刘清泰 陈锦

sentences.zh: 李國英，漢軍正紅旗人，初籍遼東。

translations.literal: Li Guoying, a man of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guoying belonged to the Han Army Bordered Red Banner and was originally registered in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 仕明隸左良玉部下，官至總兵。

translations.literal: He served the Ming under Zuo Liangyu and rose to the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he served under Zuo Liangyu and eventually became a regional commander.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，與良玉子夢庚來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he came to surrender with Liangyu's son Menggeng.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 (1645), he surrendered together with Liangyu's son Menggeng.

sentences.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格下四川，討張獻忠，授成都總兵。

translations.literal: In the third year, he followed Prince Su Hoge into Sichuan to campaign against Zhang Xianzhong and was appointed regional commander at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he marched into Sichuan with Prince Su Hoge to suppress Zhang Xianzhong and was made regional commander at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢四川巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Sichuan provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 獻忠既滅，其將孫可望、劉文秀等降於明，分遣所部王命臣等竄川南，譚弘、譚文、譚詣、楊展、劉惟明等竄川東，與李自成舊部郝搖旗、李來亨、袁宗第、劉二虎、邢十萬、馬超等遙為聲援。

translations.literal: After Xianzhong was destroyed, his generals Sun Kewang, Liu Wenxiu, and others submitted to the Ming; they sent subordinates such as Wang Mingchen to lurk in southern Sichuan, while Tan Hong, Tan Wen, Tan Yi, Yang Zhan, Liu Weiming, and others lurked in eastern Sichuan, and with Li Zicheng's former followers Hao Yaoqi, Li Laiheng, Yuan Zongdi, Liu Erhu, Xing Shiwan, Ma Chao, and others gave mutual support from afar.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Xianzhong's defeat, his generals Sun Kewang and Liu Wenxiu went over to the Ming. They sent Wang Mingchen and others into southern Sichuan and Tan Hong, Tan Wen, Tan Yi, Yang Zhan, and Liu Weiming into the east, while Li Zicheng's old commanders—Hao Yaoqi, Li Laiheng, Yuan Zongdi, Liu Erhu, Xing Shiwan, and Ma Chao—supported them from a distance.

sentences.zh: 弘犯保寧，國英擊敗之。

translations.literal: Hong attacked Baoning; Guoying defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan Hong attacked Baoning, Guoying routed him.

sentences.zh: 命臣據順慶，國英分兵三道，水陸並進，克其城，獲其將李先德、硃朝國等。

translations.literal: Mingchen held Shunqing; Guoying divided his forces into three columns and advanced by land and water together, took the city, and captured his generals Li Xiande, Zhu Chaoguo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mingchen held Shunqing. Guoying advanced in three columns by land and water, captured the city, and took generals Li Xiande and Zhu Chaoguo among others.

sentences.zh: 邢十萬、馬超所據地近保寧，國英偕總兵惠應詔討之，獲其將胡敬，复潼川，逐之至綿州，獲所置吏呂濟民等。

translations.literal: The territory held by Xing Shiwan and Ma Chao lay near Baoning; Guoying together with regional commander Hui Yingzhao campaigned against them, captured their general Hu Jing, recovered Tongchuan, pursued them to Mianzhou, and captured the officials they had installed, including Lü Jimin.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shiwan and Ma Chao held ground near Baoning. Guoying and regional commander Hui Yingzhao attacked them, took their general Hu Jing, recovered Tongchuan, drove them to Mianzhou, and captured officials they had appointed, including Lü Jimin.

sentences.zh: 尋招惟明、展來降，遂下綿州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he induced Weiming and Zhan to surrender, and then took Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon induced Liu Weiming and Yang Zhan to surrender and then captured Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，進復安縣，克彰明，破曲山關，徇石泉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he advanced to recover An County, captured Zhangming, broke Qushan Pass, and subjugated Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he recovered An County, took Zhangming, broke through Qushan Pass, and subdued Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 有謝光祖者，據寨抗，師行，遣兵破斬之。

translations.literal: A certain Xie Guangzu held a stockade in resistance; as the army marched, Guoying sent troops to defeat and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Guangzu held a stockade in defiance, Guoying sent troops on the march to defeat and execute him.

sentences.zh: 七年，遣副將曹純忠、劉漢臣徇​​川北諸郡縣，設伏擊斬寇渠老鐵匠、黃鷂子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he dispatched deputy commanders Cao Chunzhong and Liu Hanchen to subdue the prefectures and counties of northern Sichuan, set an ambush, and killed the bandit leaders Old Ironsmith and Yellow Oriole.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he sent deputy commanders Cao Chunzhong and Liu Hanchen to pacify the northern Sichuan prefectures and counties, ambushed and killed the rebel chiefs Old Ironsmith and Yellow Oriole.

sentences.zh: 九年，可望、文秀大舉寇保寧，橫列十五里，勢張甚。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Kewang and Wenxiu launched a major attack on Baoning, arrayed for fifteen li, and their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Sun Kewang and Liu Wenxiu invaded Baoning in force, their line stretching fifteen li, with overwhelming momentum.

sentences.zh: 國英督兵搗其中堅，別遣兵出間道擊其後，大破之，授世職二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: Guoying directed the troops to strike their center, separately sent forces by a hidden route to attack their rear, and inflicted a great defeat; he was granted the hereditary rank of second-class Adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: Guoying led a thrust at their center while another column took a bypath and struck their rear, winning a crushing victory. He received the hereditary rank of second-class Adahafan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was given the additional title of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 時可望等破成都，重慶、夔州、嘉定皆為明守。

translations.literal: At that time Kewang and others had taken Chengdu; Chongqing, Kuizhou, and Jiading were all held by the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: By then Kewang's forces had taken Chengdu, while Chongqing, Kuizhou, and Jiading remained in Ming hands.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂、李國翰駐軍漢中，國英請敕進兵。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui and Li Guohan stationed troops at Hanzhong; Guoying requested an imperial order to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui and Li Guohan were encamped at Hanzhong, and Guoying asked the throne for orders to advance.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢陝西四川總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was promoted to Governor-General of Shaanxi and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became governor-general of Shaanxi and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三桂等自漢中下重慶，遂趨貴州。

translations.literal: Sangui and others marched from Hanzhong down on Chongqing and then pressed toward Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui marched from Hanzhong against Chongqing and then turned toward Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 文、弘、詣、二虎等分屯忠州、萬縣，合軍攻重慶，總兵程廷俊、嚴自明御之，敗走。

translations.literal: Wen, Hong, Yi, Erhu, and others garrisoned separately at Zhongzhou and Wan County, united their armies to attack Chongqing, and regional commanders Cheng Tingjun and Yan Ziming defended; the attackers were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Wen, Tan Hong, Tan Yi, and Liu Erhu held Zhongzhou and Wan County, then joined forces against Chongqing. Regional commanders Cheng Tingjun and Yan Ziming drove them off.

sentences.zh: 文又合十三家兵逼重慶，國英自保寧赴援，次合江，詣殺文以降。

translations.literal: Wen again united the Thirteen Families' troops to press Chongqing; Guoying came from Baoning to relieve the city, halted at Hejiang, and Yi killed Wen and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Wen again rallied the Thirteen Families against Chongqing. Guoying marched from Baoning to relieve the city and halted at Hejiang, where Tan Yi killed Tan Wen and submitted.

sentences.zh: 國英入城安撫，弘亦與其將郝承裔、陳達先後出降。

translations.literal: Guoying entered the city to pacify it; Hong also, with his generals Hao Chengyi and Chen Da, surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Guoying entered the city to restore order, and Tan Hong followed with his generals Hao Chengyi and Chen Da in successive surrenders.

sentences.zh: 文所部猶據涪、忠二州，國英遣總兵王明德擊破之。

translations.literal: Wen's remaining forces still held Fu and Zhong prefectures; Guoying sent regional commander Wang Mingde to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's troops still held Fu and Zhong prefectures until Guoying sent regional commander Wang Mingde to break them.

sentences.zh: 十七年，承裔據雅州复叛，國英督兵至嘉定，分三道進剿，破竹箐關入，承裔走黎州，追獲之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Chengyi held Yazhou and rebelled again; Guoying led troops to Jiading, advanced in three columns to suppress him, broke through Zhuzhu Pass, Chengyi fled to Lizhou, and was captured in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Hao Chengyi seized Yazhou and rebelled again. Guoying marched to Jiading, advanced in three columns, broke through Zhuzhu Pass, pursued Chengyi to Lizhou, and captured him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，川、陝各設總督，命國英專轄四川。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, separate governors-general were established for Sichuan and Shaanxi, and Guoying was ordered to govern Sichuan alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Sichuan and Shaanxi each received their own governor-general, and Guoying was assigned to govern Sichuan exclusively.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，明石泉王奉鋡攻敘州，國英討平之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, the Ming Prince of Shiquan, Feng Xia, attacked Xuzhou; Guoying suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662) the Ming Prince of Shiquan, Feng Xia, attacked Xuzhou, and Guoying put down the rising.

sentences.zh: 時搖旗、來亨、二虎、宗第等據茅麓山，出掠四川、湖廣、陝西錯壤諸州縣。

translations.literal: At that time Yaoqi, Laiheng, Erhu, Zongdi, and others held Maolu Mountain and raided the interlocking prefectures and counties of Sichuan, Huguang, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yaoqi, Li Laiheng, Liu Erhu, and Yuan Zongdi then held Maolu Mountain and raided the border counties where Sichuan, Huguang, and Shaanxi met.

sentences.zh: 議三省合軍討之，國英疏言：「賊巢橫據險要，我師進攻，未能聯合。

translations.literal: It was proposed that the three provinces unite their armies to suppress them; Guoying memorialized: "The rebels' lair spans difficult terrain; when our armies attack, they cannot coordinate."
translations.idiomatic: A joint campaign by the three provinces was proposed. Guoying wrote: "The rebels hold rugged ground in a wide arc; when our columns attack, they cannot link up."

sentences.zh: 宜豫會師期，分道併入，使賊三路受敵，彼此不暇兼顧。

translations.literal: We should fix a rendezvous date in advance and enter by separate routes together, so that the rebels are attacked on three sides and cannot attend to one another.
translations.idiomatic: We should set a rendezvous date and advance on separate routes so the rebels face attack on three fronts and cannot shift forces between them.

sentences.zh: 一路既平，就近會師，賊可盡殲。

translations.literal: Once one route is pacified, the armies should join nearby, and the rebels can be annihilated entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Once one column clears its sector, the armies can unite nearby and wipe the rebels out.

sentences.zh: 」上命將軍穆里瑪、圖海將禁旅討之，國英與西安將軍富喀禪、副都統都敏會剿。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Generals Muli Ma and Tu Hai to lead the Banner guards in the campaign; Guoying joined with Xi'an General Fukatan and Vice Commander-in-chief Du Min in joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Generals Muli Ma and Tu Hai to lead the guards in the campaign, while Guoying coordinated with Xi'an General Fukatan and Vice Commander-in-chief Du Min.

sentences.zh: 明年，督兵進巫山，趨陳家坡，破二虎壘。

translations.literal: The next year, he led troops into Wushan, pressed toward Chenjiapo, and broke Erhu's fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he advanced through Wushan toward Chenjiapo and stormed Liu Erhu's stronghold.

sentences.zh: 二虎走死，搖旗、宗第夜遁。

translations.literal: Erhu fled and died; Yaoqi and Zongdi escaped by night.
translations.idiomatic: Erhu fled to his death while Yaoqi and Zongdi slipped away under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 總兵梁加琦、佐領巴達世逐之至黃草坪，獲搖旗、宗第及所置吏洪育鰲等。

translations.literal: Regional commander Liang Jiaqi and company commander Badashi pursued them to Huangcaoping and captured Yaoqi, Zongdi, and the officials they had installed, including Hong Yu'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Liang Jiaqi and company commander Badashi ran them down at Huangcaoping and took Yaoqi, Zongdi, and their appointee Hong Yu'ao among others.

sentences.zh: 又遣總兵李良楨破小尖寨，獲明東安王盛蒗，叛將賀珍子道寧以所部降。

translations.literal: He also sent regional commander Li Liangzhen to storm Xiaojian Stockade, captured the Ming Prince of Dong'an, Sheng Lang, and the rebel He Zhen's son Daoning surrendered with his following.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent regional commander Li Liangzhen against Xiaojian Stockade, captured the Ming Prince of Dong'an Sheng Lang, and the rebel He Zhen's son Daoning surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「全川底定，裁留通省兵四萬五千名，以馬二、步一戰守各半定額。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he memorialized: "All Sichuan is settled; retain forty-five thousand troops for the whole province, with a quota of two-thirds cavalry and one-third infantry, half for campaigning and half for garrison."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he wrote: "Sichuan is fully pacified. Keep forty-five thousand provincial troops on a two-to-one horse-to-foot ratio, split evenly between field and garrison duty."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，諡勤襄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died; his posthumous title was Qinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year and was given the posthumous name Qinxiang (Diligent and Assisting).

sentences.zh: 七年，追敘國英功，授世職一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Guoying's merits were reviewed posthumously and the hereditary rank of first-class Ashanihafan was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his service was commemorated and his line received the hereditary rank of first-class Ashanihafan.

sentences.zh: 孫永昇，襲職。

translations.literal: His grandson Yongsheng inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yongsheng inherited the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，官南陽總兵。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign, he served as regional commander at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he served as regional commander at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 坐事戍軍台。

translations.literal: For an offense he was banished to a military colony.
translations.idiomatic: After a conviction he was sent to garrison duty on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 世宗念國英前勞，召還，洊擢至工部尚書。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor, mindful of Guoying's earlier service, recalled him and repeatedly promoted him to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Guoying's earlier service, the Yongzheng Emperor recalled him and promoted him step by step to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以永昇從子時敏襲職。

translations.literal: Yongsheng's nephew Shimin was made to inherit the office.
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng's nephew Shimin inherited the hereditary post in his place.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封一等男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, the rank was fixed as first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong the line was fixed at first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 劉武元，字鎮籓，漢軍鑲紅旗人，初籍遼東。

translations.literal: Liu Wuyuan, style Zhenfan, a man of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuyuan (style Zhenfan), of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 仕明官游擊，佐祖大壽守大凌河，天聰五年，從大壽出降。

translations.literal: He served the Ming as a battalion commander, assisted his grandfather Zu Dashou in defending Dalinghe, and in the fifth year of Tiancong followed Dashou in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he was a battalion commander and helped his grandfather Zu Dashou hold Dalinghe; in Tiancong 5 (1631) he surrendered with Dashou.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年，授刑部參政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongde, he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 6 (1641) he was made Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，改授甲喇額真，予世職三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was reassigned as jalan ejen and granted the hereditary rank of third-class jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 (1644) he became a jalan ejen and received the hereditary rank of third-class jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 二年，授天津兵備道。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed Tianjin military preparedness commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Tianjin military preparedness commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢南贛巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Nan'gan provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to governor of southern Jiangxi (Nan'gan).

sentences.zh: 四年，遣副將劉伯祿、徐啟仁等剿捕瑞金、石城，興國、龍安，寧都、上猶諸州縣土寇，克魚骨、蓮花、丁田、鉤刀嘴諸寨，斬其渠葉南枝、劉志諭、劉飛等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he sent deputy commanders Liu Bolu, Xu Qiren, and others to suppress bandits in the prefectures and counties of Ruijin, Shicheng, Xingguo, Long'an, Ningdu, and Shangyou, captured the stockades of Yugu, Lianhua, Dingtian, and Goudaozui, and beheaded their leaders Ye Nanzhi, Liu Zhiyu, Liu Fei, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he sent deputy commanders Liu Bolu and Xu Qiren to suppress local bandits in Ruijin, Shicheng, Xingguo, Long'an, Ningdu, and Shangyou, took the stockades at Yugu, Lianhua, Dingtian, and Goudaozui, and executed ringleaders Ye Nanzhi, Liu Zhiyu, and Liu Fei.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，金聲桓、王得仁以南昌叛，江西諸郡縣皆附，外連閩、粵，贛州介其間。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Jin Shengwan and Wang Deren rebelled at Nanchang; the prefectures and counties of Jiangxi all joined them, they linked outward with Fujian and Guangdong, and Ganzhou lay between.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Jin Shengwan and Wang Deren rebelled at Nanchang. Jiangxi's prefectures fell in behind them, they linked with Fujian and Guangdong, and Ganzhou stood in the middle.

sentences.zh: 武元召諸將歃血誓，得仁以二十萬人來攻，啟仁出降，圍合。

translations.literal: Wuyuan summoned the generals to swear an oath in blood; Deren came to attack with two hundred thousand men, Qiren surrendered, and the encirclement closed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan had his generals swear a blood oath. Deren attacked with two hundred thousand men, Qiren defected, and the siege closed around the city.

sentences.zh: 武元城守三月，糧盡，斥家財佐軍，勵士卒奮戰，遂破得仁兵。

translations.literal: Wuyuan defended the city for three months; when provisions were exhausted, he spent his family wealth to support the army, urged the soldiers to fight fiercely, and finally broke Deren's forces.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan held the city for three months. When grain ran out he poured out his family fortune for the troops, roused them to fight, and finally routed Deren's army.

sentences.zh: 得仁退屯東山，引武元空城出戰，將設伏邀擊。

translations.literal: Deren withdrew to camp at Dongshan, lured Wuyuan out with an empty city to give battle, and intended to set an ambush to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Deren fell back to Dongshan, baited Wuyuan out with an apparently empty city, and prepared an ambush.

sentences.zh: 武元知其謀，天未明，兵數百持炬為前驅，得仁兵望見，伏盡出，力戰，得仁中創遁。

translations.literal: Wuyuan knew his plan; before dawn several hundred soldiers with torches went ahead as vanguard; Deren's troops saw them, the ambushers all came out, fought fiercely, and Deren was wounded and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan saw through the trap. Before dawn he sent several hundred men with torches as a vanguard; Deren's troops took the bait, the ambushers sprang out, and in the hard fighting Deren was wounded and fled.

sentences.zh: 聲桓聞我師至九江，謀退保南昌，武元出奇兵襲其後，敗之太湖港，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: Shengwan heard that our army had reached Jiujiang and planned to withdraw to hold Nanchang; Wuyuan sent a surprise force to strike his rear, defeated him at Taihu Harbor, and killed and captured beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengwan heard imperial troops had reached Jiujiang and planned to fall back on Nanchang, Wuyuan struck his rear with a surprise column, routed him at Taihu Harbor, and took a vast toll in killed and captured.

sentences.zh: 十月，叛將李成棟復來攻，眾號百萬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the rebel Li Chengdong attacked again, his force claiming a million men.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebel Li Chengdong attacked again with a host said to number a million.

sentences.zh: 武元先出兵數百撓之，夜縋城出死士劫破十餘壘，遂令諸將分兵東、西、南三門出戰，大破之，成棟以數騎走。

translations.literal: Wuyuan first sent out several hundred men to harass them; at night he lowered dare-to-die troops from the wall to raid and break more than ten camps; then he ordered the generals to divide forces and sally from the east, west, and south gates, inflicted a great defeat, and Chengdong fled with a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan first sent out a few hundred men to skirmish, then at night lowered assault troops who stormed more than ten camps. He ordered his generals to sally from the east, west, and south gates, won a crushing victory, and Chengdong fled with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加右都御史，兼兵部侍郎，賜紫貂冠服、甲胄、佩刀、鞍馬。

translations.literal: Merit was reviewed: he was given the additional titles of Censor-in-chief of the Right and Vice Minister of War, and was granted a sable cap and robe, armor, a girdle sword, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Censor-in-chief of the Right and Vice Minister of War and received a sable cap and robe, armor, sword, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 六年，征南​​大將軍譚泰既克南昌，遣梅勒額真覺善等與武元會師，克信豐，成棟宵遁，墮水死。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, after the southern expedition commander-in-chief Tan Tai had taken Nanchang, he sent meiren ejen Jueshan and others to join Wuyuan; they took Xinfeng, Chengdong fled by night, fell into the water, and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after southern expedition commander Tan Tai took Nanchang, he sent meiren ejen Jueshan to join Wuyuan. They captured Xinfeng; Chengdong fled by night, fell into the river, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 武元分遣副將先啟玉、參將鮑虎、游擊左雲龍等捕成棟餘黨，定瑞金、雩都、崇義諸縣。

translations.literal: Wuyuan separately sent deputy commanders Xian Qiyu, brigade commanders Bao Hu, battalion commander Zuo Yunlong, and others to hunt down Chengdong's remnants and pacify the counties of Ruijin, Yudu, and Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan sent deputy commander Xian Qiyu, brigade commander Bao Hu, battalion commander Zuo Yunlong, and others to mop up Chengdong's remnants and secure Ruijin, Yudu, and Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 進攻梅嶺，破木城五，獲成棟將劉治國。

translations.literal: He advanced against Meiling, broke five wooden forts, and captured Chengdong's general Liu Zhiguo.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Meiling, stormed five wooden forts, and captured Chengdong's general Liu Zhiguo.

sentences.zh: 七年，平南王尚可喜徇廣東，師自南安入，武元遣副將栗養志以兵從，克南雄、韶州二府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, subjugated Guangdong; the army entered from Nan'an, and Wuyuan sent deputy commander Li Yangzhi with troops to follow, capturing the two prefectures of Nanxiong and Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi campaigned in Guangdong. The army entered from Nan'an; Wuyuan sent deputy commander Li Yangzhi in support, and they took Nanxiong and Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 又遣副將高進庫，游擊楊繼、洪起元等剿寧都土寇彭順慶，副將楊遇明、劉伯祿、賈熊、董大用等剿大庾土寇羅榮。

translations.literal: He also sent deputy commander Gao Jinku, battalion commanders Yang Ji and Hong Qiyuan, and others to suppress the Ningdu bandit Peng Shunqing; and deputy commanders Yang Yuming, Liu Bolu, Jia Xiong, Dong Dayong, and others to suppress the Dayu bandit Luo Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent deputy commander Gao Jinku and battalion commanders Yang Ji and Hong Qiyuan against the Ningdu bandit Peng Shunqing, and deputy commanders Yang Yuming, Liu Bolu, Jia Xiong, and Dong Dayong against the Dayu bandit Luo Rong.

sentences.zh: 順慶應聲桓為亂，自號軍門，窺伺郡邑；

translations.literal: Shunqing had answered Shengwan's rebellion, styled himself Military Gate, and watched for chances against the prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shunqing had joined Shengwan's revolt, styled himself Military Gate, and eyed the surrounding prefectures;

sentences.zh: 榮自明季倡亂楚、粵間，自號五軍都督，聚眾數万，阻山結寨二十餘，四出劫掠：至是皆就戮。

translations.literal: Rong had stirred rebellion between Chu and Yue since the late Ming, styled himself Commander-in-chief of the Five Armies, gathered tens of thousands, blocked the mountains and built more than twenty stockades, and raided on all sides: by this time all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rong had raised trouble between Huguang and Guangdong since the late Ming, called himself Commander-in-chief of the Five Armies, mustered tens of thousands in more than twenty mountain stockades, and raided widely—all were put to death on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加太子太保、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Merit was reviewed: he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 遇恩詔，進世職一等阿達哈哈番又一拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: On an amnesty edict, his hereditary rank was advanced to first-class Adahafan with an additional Tosahafan.
translations.idiomatic: On an amnesty edict his line was raised to first-class Adahafan with an additional Tosahafan.

sentences.zh: 十年，引疾還京。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he cited illness and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he pleaded illness and returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，贈少保，諡明靖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Mingjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year and was posthumously made Junior Guardian with the posthumous name Mingjing (Bright and Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 瀇，武元長子，襲職。

translations.literal: Yuan, Wuyuan's eldest son, inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, his eldest son, inherited the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 疏請追敘武元贛州全城功，進二等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting retrospective recognition of Wuyuan's merit in holding Ganzhou intact, and the rank was advanced to second-class Ashanihafan.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to commemorate Wuyuan's defense of Ganzhou, and the line was raised to second-class Ashanihafan.

sentences.zh: 官至副都統。

translations.literal: He rose to the office of vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 浩，武元次子。

translations.literal: Hao, Wuyuan's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was Wuyuan's second son.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，官廣西潯州知府。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, he served as prefect of Xunzhou in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he was prefect of Xunzhou in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 孫延齡叛，城陷被戕，並及其子中樞、中梁、中柱、中楫。

translations.literal: When Sun Yanling rebelled, the city fell and he was killed, together with his sons Zhongshu, Zhongliang, Zhongzhu, and Zhongji.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Yanling rebelled the city fell and he was slain, together with his sons Zhongshu, Zhongliang, Zhongzhu, and Zhongji.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太僕卿。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court he was posthumously made Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 庫禮，喜塔臘氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ku Li, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ku Li of the Xitala clan was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 太祖創業初，其四世祖昂果都理巴顏來歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taizu's founding enterprise, his fourth-generation ancestor Anguoduli Bayan came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the earliest days of the Taizu's rise, his fourth-generation ancestor Anguoduli Bayan submitted.

sentences.zh: 庫禮事太宗。

translations.literal: Ku Li served the Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Ku Li served the Taizong (Hong Taiji).

sentences.zh: 崇德初，徵朝鮮兵從征伐，命庫禮將其軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongde, Korean troops were levied for the campaigns; Ku Li was ordered to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongde Korean troops were called up for the campaigns, and Ku Li was placed in command.

sentences.zh: 五年，睿親王多爾袞等伐明，圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Prince Rui Dorgon and others campaigned against the Ming and besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Prince Rui Dorgon and others invaded the Ming and besieged Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 上遣戶部參政碩詹使朝鮮，發水師五千人、米萬斛詣大凌河，庫禮與梅勒額真洪尼哈將三十人導。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Vice Minister of Revenue Shuozhan as envoy to Korea to dispatch five thousand naval troops and ten thousand hu of grain to Dalinghe; Ku Li and meiren ejen Hongniha led thirty men as guides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister of Revenue Shuozhan to Korea to raise five thousand sailors and ten thousand hu of grain for Dalinghe; Ku Li and meiren ejen Hongniha guided them with thirty men.

sentences.zh: 六年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗圍錦州，克其郛，斬八百餘級。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala in besieging Jinzhou, took its outer wall, and beheaded more than eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Prince Zheng Jirhala at Jinzhou, took the outer defenses, and killed more than eight hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 復與噶布什賢噶喇依昂邦薩穆什喀攻松山北崖，庫禮以朝鮮兵二百餘先登。

translations.literal: Again with gabushi xian gara-i angbang Samushka he attacked the north cliff of Songshan; Ku Li with more than two hundred Korean troops was first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined gabushi xian Samushka against the north cliff of Songshan, and Ku Li led more than two hundred Korean troops in the first ascent.

sentences.zh: 科爾沁部人或降於明，發砲中庫禮手，庫禮不為動，督戰益力，卒破明兵。

translations.literal: Some of the Khorchin tribesmen had surrendered to the Ming and fired cannon that struck Ku Li's hand; Ku Li did not stir, directed the battle with greater force, and finally broke the Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: Some Khorchin tribesmen had gone over to the Ming and a cannon ball struck Ku Li's hand, but he did not flinch, pressed the fight harder, and finally routed the Ming force.

sentences.zh: 攻松山，明兵擊正紅、鑲藍二旗分守地，庫禮與左翼將領勒卜忒擊之，明兵引卻。

translations.literal: In the attack on Songshan, Ming troops struck the sectors garrisoned by the Bordered Red and Bordered Blue Banners; Ku Li with the left-wing commander Lebute struck them, and the Ming troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Songshan, Ming troops hit the sectors held by the Bordered Red and Bordered Blue Banners; Ku Li and left-wing commander Lebute counterattacked and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 以功授世職牛錄章京，賚所獲牲畜。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the hereditary rank of niru janggin and rewarded with livestock taken in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received the hereditary rank of niru janggin and a grant of livestock from the spoils.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢戶部參政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 順治初，改戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, he was reassigned as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he became Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 論定都功，加半個前程。

translations.literal: When merit for fixing the capital was reviewed, he was given half a qian-cheng advancement.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in establishing the capital he received half a qian-cheng advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 旋坐阿豫親王多鐸指，集視八旗女子，論罰鍰。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on Prince Yu Dorgon's accusation that he had assembled the women of the Eight Banners for inspection, he was sentenced to a fine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Prince Yu Dorgon accused him of assembling Banner women for inspection, and he was fined.

sentences.zh: 二年，命如淮安總理漕儲。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was ordered to go to Huai'an to oversee grain transport and storage.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was sent to Huai'an to oversee the grain transport system.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，鹽城土寇竊發，庫禮與漕運總督楊聲遠親往撫慰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year, bandits broke out secretly in Yancheng; Ku Li and Grain Transport Governor-General Yang Shengyuan went in person to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year bandits rose in Yancheng; Ku Li and grain transport governor-general Yang Shengyuan went in person to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其渠周文山等以八百人夜襲淮安，自夾城東門缺口入，攻庫禮官廨。

translations.literal: Before long, their leader Zhou Wenshan and others with eight hundred men raided Huai'an by night, entered through a breach at the east gate of the barbican, and attacked Ku Li's official residence.
translations.idiomatic: Before long their leader Zhou Wenshan led eight hundred men in a night raid on Huai'an, broke in through a gap at the barbican's east gate, and assaulted Ku Li's yamen.

sentences.zh: 庫禮率中軍張大治、旗鼓王國印將帳下卒數十人御之，其妻盡出廨儲矢，僕婢齎送助戰，眾皆一當百，自醜至辰，所殺傷過當。

translations.literal: Ku Li led Central Army Zhang Dazhi and standard-bearer Wang Guoyin with several dozen soldiers from his staff to defend; his wife brought out all the arrows stored in the yamen, servants and maids carried them forward to aid the fight, each man fought as one against a hundred, from the chou hour to the chen hour, and the killed and wounded were beyond proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Ku Li led Central Army Zhang Dazhi and standard-bearer Wang Guoyin with a few dozen household troops to hold them off. His wife emptied the yamen's arrow stores; servants and maids ferried ammunition to the fight. Each defender fought like a hundred from the chou hour until chen, and the enemy's losses were staggering.

sentences.zh: 文山等潰走，逐斬百八十餘級，盡收其印劄、軍械，城賴以全。

translations.literal: Wenshan and others fled in rout; pursuing, they beheaded more than one hundred eighty, recovered all their seals and letters and military equipment, and the city was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshan's men broke and fled; the pursuers cut down more than one hundred eighty of them, seized their seals, credentials, and arms, and the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 有稱明益王者，奉唐王聿鍵隆武號，屯廟灣，有眾數千、舟百餘，將攻淮安，庫禮與聲遠等計，設伏以待。

translations.literal: One who styled himself Prince Yiwang of the Ming, honoring the Tang prince Zhu Yujian with the Longwu reign title, encamped at Miaowan with several thousand followers and more than a hundred boats, was about to attack Huai'an; Ku Li and Shengyuan and others planned and set an ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: A man claiming to be the Ming Prince Yiwang, upholding the Longwu reign of the Tang prince Zhu Yujian, held Miaowan with several thousand men and over a hundred boats and was poised to strike Huai'an. Ku Li and Yang Shengyuan laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 敵舟揚帆直上，至車家橋，伏發，水陸夾擊，敵死者過半，餘眾走還廟灣。

translations.literal: The enemy boats sailed straight up with full sail; at Chejia Bridge the ambush was sprung, land and water forces struck together, more than half the enemy died, and the remainder fled back to Miaowan.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fleet sailed upstream to Chejia Bridge, where the trap was sprung. Land and river forces struck together; more than half were killed and the rest fled back to Miaowan.

sentences.zh: 固山額真張大猷、巡撫陳之龍以師從之，敵據劉莊場，為屯凡十，以次剿撫，旬日乃盡定。

translations.literal: Gushan ejen Zhang Dayou and Governor Chen Zhilong followed with troops; the enemy held Liuzhuangchang with ten camps in all, which were suppressed and pacified in succession, and within ten days all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gushan ejen Zhang Dayou and governor Chen Zhilong followed with troops. The enemy held Liuzhuangchang in ten camps, which were subdued one by one until all was quiet within ten days.

sentences.zh: 考滿，進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: At the completion of his performance review, he was advanced to third-class Adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: When his term review ended, he was raised to third-class Adahafan.

sentences.zh: 尋召還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 七年，致仕，復進一等阿達哈哈番加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he retired from office and was again advanced to first-class Adahafan with an additional Tosahafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retired and was again promoted to first-class Adahafan with an additional Tosahafan.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡僖恪。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Xike.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Xike (Joyful and Respectful).

sentences.zh: 胡全才，山西文水人。

translations.literal: Hu Quancai, a native of Wenshui in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Quancai was a native of Wenshui, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官兵部主事。

translations.literal: A Chongzhen-era jinshi, he served the Ming as a principal secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign, he had been a principal secretary in the Ming Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，固山額真葉臣定山西，疏薦，起原官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, when gushan ejen Ye Chen pacified Shanxi, Quancai was recommended in a memorial and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, after gushan ejen Ye Chen pacified Shanxi, Quancai was recommended and restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 二年，自郎中授陝西漢羌道，駐漢中。

translations.literal: In the second year, from director he was appointed Han-Qiang circuit intendant in Shaanxi, stationed at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he moved from director to Han-Qiang circuit intendant in Shaanxi, based at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時叛將賀珍為亂，全才上官，撫綏彫瘵，安集流亡。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel He Zhen was in revolt; Quancai took up his post, soothed the ravaged land, and settled the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel He Zhen was then in revolt. Quancai took office, soothed the war-ravaged region, and resettled refugees.

sentences.zh: 招明將趙光遠部曲齊升、王明德、李世勳等來降，盡收其軍械，與知府楊可經等練士卒，聚芻糧為備。

translations.literal: He induced the Ming general Zhao Guangyuan's followers Qi Sheng, Wang Mingde, Li Shixun, and others to surrender, collected all their arms, and with Prefect Yang Kejing and others drilled troops and gathered fodder and grain in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: He induced Zhao Guangyuan's followers Qi Sheng, Wang Mingde, and Li Shixun to surrender, seized their arms, and with prefect Yang Kejing drilled troops and stockpiled grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 珍突至圍城，升等奮勇衝擊，世勳中流矢死。

translations.literal: Zhen suddenly arrived and besieged the city; Sheng and others charged out fiercely, and Shixun was struck by an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen suddenly appeared and besieged the city. Qi Sheng led a fierce sortie, but Li Shixun was killed by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 城守三十餘日，援師至，珍遁走，漢中得全。

translations.literal: The city was held for more than thirty days; relief arrived, Zhen fled, and Hanzhong was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The city held for more than thirty days until relief arrived; Zhen fled and Hanzhong was saved.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎趙京仕疏言漢中重地，宜設巡撫，且薦全才才稱仕。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works Zhao Jingshi memorialized that Hanzhong was a vital place and ought to have a governor, and also recommended that Quancai's talent matched the office.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works Zhao Jingshi argued that Hanzhong was strategically vital and needed a governor, and that Quancai was fit for the post.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢寧夏巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Ningxia provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became governor of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏請頒本朝律典及性理、通鑑諸書，令士子誦習。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he memorialized requesting that the dynasty's legal code and books such as the Neo-Confucian classics and Comprehensive Mirror be issued for scholars to study.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked that the dynasty's code and standard texts—the Neo-Confucian classics and Comprehensive Mirror—be distributed for scholars to study.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「寧夏舊額兵三萬有奇，設總兵及中軍副將分統之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Ningxia's former troop quota was a little more than thirty thousand, with a regional commander and a central-army deputy commander to command them separately.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Ningxia once fielded a little over thirty thousand troops under a regional commander and a central-army deputy commander."

sentences.zh: 其後兵裁及半，罷中軍副將。

translations.literal: Later the troops were cut by half and the central-army deputy commander was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later the force was halved and the central-army deputy post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 往者總兵應徵發，叛將王元遂乘隙戕巡撫焦安民為亂。

translations.literal: Formerly when the regional commander was called out on campaign, the rebel Wang Yuan seized the chance to kill Governor Jiao Anmin and raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the regional commander was called away on campaign, the rebel Wang Yuan had killed Governor Jiao Anmin and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 宜復舊制，廣兵額，設中軍，調徵興慶副將馬寧嘗擒斬王元，請仍補斯缺。

translations.literal: The old system should be restored, troop quotas expanded, a central army established, and Deputy Commander Ma Ning of Xingqing—who once captured and executed Wang Yuan—be summoned to fill that post again.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restoring the old system, expanding the rolls, reinstating the central-army command, and recalling Xingqing deputy commander Ma Ning, who had once captured and killed Wang Yuan, to fill the vacancy.

sentences.zh: 」下部議，並如所請。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries for deliberation, and all was granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved every point.

sentences.zh: 元黨馬德既降复叛，全才與總兵劉芳名發兵討誅之。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan's follower Ma De had surrendered and rebelled again; Quancai with regional commander Liu Fangming sent troops to suppress and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan's follower Ma De had submitted and rebelled again; Quancai and regional commander Liu Fangming marched out and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 語詳芳名傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in Fangming's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Fangming's biography.

sentences.zh: 是歲山、陝蝗見，全才為捕蝗法授州縣吏，蝗至，如法捕輒盡，不傷稼。

translations.literal: That year locusts appeared in Shaanxi and Shanxi; Quancai taught locust-catching methods to the prefectural and county officials; when locusts came, they were caught by the method until none remained, without harm to the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts appeared that year in Shaanxi and Shanxi. Quancai taught officials his locust-catching method; when swarms came, they were destroyed without crop damage.

sentences.zh: 因以其法上聞，命傳示諸直省。

translations.literal: He therefore reported the method upward, and the emperor ordered it transmitted to all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the method to the throne, and the court ordered it circulated to every province.

sentences.zh: 初，全才任漢羌道時，令凡受賀珍劄付者，許自首，仍予劄付如其官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Quancai was Han-Qiang intendant, he ordered that all who had received credentials from He Zhen might confess and still receive credentials matching their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Han-Qiang intendant, he had allowed anyone holding He Zhen's credentials to surrender and keep equivalent appointments.

sentences.zh: 旋揭告漢羌總兵尤可望苛罰冒餉，藏匿偽官，可望即以擅給劄付訐全才，並坐罷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he exposed Han-Qiang regional commander You Kewang for harsh fines, false muster rolls, and hiding pretended officials; Kewang then impeached Quancai for giving credentials without authority, and Quancai was dismissed on both charges.
translations.idiomatic: He then exposed regional commander You Kewang for extortion, padded rolls, and sheltering false officials. Kewang retaliated by accusing Quancai of issuing credentials without authority, and Quancai was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 全才詣部自陳，部議以全才功大罪小，复除江西饒南道。

translations.literal: Quancai went to the ministry to explain himself; the ministry ruled that his merit was great and his fault small, and he was reappointed to Raonan circuit in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Quancai pleaded his case at the ministry, which ruled his service outweighed his fault and reappointed him to Raonan circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十年，經略洪承疇奏薦，令從征湖南。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou recommended him, and he was ordered to follow the Hunan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou recommended him for the Hunan campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋命撫治鄖陽，提督軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to administer Xunyang and supervise military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made administrator of Xunyang with authority over military affairs.

sentences.zh: 李自成將郝搖旗、劉體純等降於明，及明桂王走南徼，遂屯聚房、竹群山間為盜。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng's generals Hao Yaoqi and Liu Tichun and others had submitted to the Ming; when the Ming Prince of Gui fled to the southern marches, they gathered in the Fang and Zhu Mountains as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's generals Hao Yaoqi and Liu Tichun had gone over to the Ming; when the Prince of Gui fled south, they turned bandit in the Fang and Zhu Mountains.

sentences.zh: 全才分兵扼衝要，馳察穀城、南漳諸地形勢，檄諸將進討，戰屢勝。

translations.literal: Quancai divided troops to hold the strategic passes, rode out to survey the terrain of Gucheng, Nanzhang, and other places, and ordered the generals forward; battles were repeatedly won.
translations.idiomatic: Quancai blocked the key passes, reconnoitered Gucheng and Nanzhang, ordered his generals forward, and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 十三年，明桂王所置總兵李企晟入鄖陽，與搖旗等合，全才遣諸將硃光祚等密捕之，執企晟。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Li Qisheng, regional commander appointed by the Ming Prince of Gui, entered Xunyang and joined Yaoqi and others; Quancai sent the generals Zhu Guangzuo and others to seize him secretly and took Qisheng prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Ming Prince of Gui's appointee Li Qisheng entered Xunyang and joined Yaoqi. Quancai's generals Zhu Guangzuo and others seized him in a covert operation.

sentences.zh: 旋擢湖廣總督，卒官，贈兵部尚書，諡勤毅。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Huguang governor-general, died in office, was posthumously made Minister of War, and given the posthumous title Qinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor-general of Huguang, died in office, and was posthumously honored as Minister of War with the name Qinyi (Diligent and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 申朝紀，漢軍鑲藍旗人，初籍遼東。

translations.literal: Shen Chaoji, a man of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chaoji, of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，授刑部啟心郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong, he was appointed a censorial secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 he became a censorial secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 文館硃延慶疏陳時事，薦朝紀溫雅正直，練達世務，處家儉，守身約，訥言敏行，足任鴻鉅。

translations.literal: Zhu Yanqing of the Literary Institute memorialized on current affairs, recommending Chaoji as gentle and upright, experienced in worldly affairs, frugal in household management, strict in personal conduct, taciturn yet quick in action, and fit for great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanqing of the Literary Institute praised current affairs and recommended Chaoji as upright, experienced, frugal, disciplined, reserved yet decisive—fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，賜人戶、牲畜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, he was granted households and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he received households and livestock as grants.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授河南河北道，駐懷慶，李自成之黨二萬餘來犯，朝紀登陴守禦，晝夜不少懈，有渠乘白馬薄壕，麾眾攻城，朝紀舉砲殪之，賊悉驚竄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was appointed Henan north-of-the-Yellow River circuit intendant, stationed at Huaiqing; more than twenty thousand of Li Zicheng's followers came to attack; Chaoji mounted the walls to defend day and night without slackening; a bandit chief on a white horse pressed close to the moat and directed the masses to assault the walls; Chaoji fired cannon and killed him, and the bandits all fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he was made intendant of Henan north of the Yellow River at Huaiqing. More than twenty thousand of Li Zicheng's men attacked; Chaoji held the walls day and night. A chief on a white horse pressed the moat and ordered the assault; Chaoji's cannon killed him and the rebels scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷江南布政使，擢山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Jiangnan provincial administration commissioner and promoted to Shanxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became Jiangnan administration commissioner and then Shanxi governor.

sentences.zh: 三年，疏言：「驛遞累民，始自明季，計糧養馬，按畝役夫。

translations.literal: In the third year, he memorialized: "The courier system burdens the people, beginning from the late Ming, calculating grain to maintain horses and assigning laborers by mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he wrote: "The courier system has burdened the people since the late Ming, with grain levies for horses and labor assessed by acreage."

sentences.zh: 臣禁革驛遞濫應、里甲私派。

translations.literal: Your servant has forbidden unauthorized courier requisitions and private levies by village heads.
translations.idiomatic: I have banned unauthorized courier demands and private levies by village heads.

sentences.zh: 請飭勒石各驛，永遠遵守，俾毋蹈前轍。

translations.literal: I request that each station be ordered to carve this in stone and observe it forever, so as not to repeat past abuses.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each post inscribe these rules in stone and observe them permanently so past abuses are not repeated.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「各省驛站銀舊額十五萬有奇，明季裁充兵餉。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The old quota of courier silver in each province was a little more than one hundred fifty thousand taels; in the late Ming it was cut to pay military rations.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that provincial courier funds had totaled more than one hundred fifty thousand taels before the late Ming cuts diverted them to military pay.

sentences.zh: 驛費不足，輒私派於民。

translations.literal: When courier funds were insufficient, they were privately levied on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls were made up by illegal levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 請敕部復原額。

translations.literal: I request that the ministry be ordered to restore the original quota.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the ministry to restore the original allocation.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「賦役全書應裁、應留諸項，請覈實詳酌，俾有司不得私徵濫派。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Items in the Complete Book of Tax and Labor that should be cut or retained should be verified and weighed in detail, so that local officials may not privately levy or over-assess.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged a careful audit of items in the Complete Book of Tax and Labor so local officials could not levy private surcharges.

sentences.zh: 」疏並下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorials were all sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All three memorials were referred to the ministries and enacted.

sentences.zh: 四年，陽城民王希堯、賈國昌等以邪教倡亂，朝紀遣中軍都司白璧同冀南道武延祚率兵捕治，悉誅希堯、國昌等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Yangcheng commoners Wang Xiyao, Jia Guochang, and others stirred rebellion with a heterodox cult; Chaoji sent Central Army Commander Bai Bi with Ji'nan circuit intendant Wu Yanzuo to lead troops to suppress them and executed Xiyao, Guochang, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Xiyao and Jia Guochang of Yangcheng raised a cult rebellion. Chaoji sent Central Army Commander Bai Bi with Ji'nan intendant Wu Yanzuo to suppress them and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 汾州營卒李本清、任自興等據永寧銅柱寨為亂，朝紀赴汾州，遣冀寧道王昌齡等率兵捕治，獲本清等，焚其寨。

translations.literal: Fenzhou garrison soldiers Li Benqing, Ren Zixing, and others held Yongning Tongzhu Stockade in rebellion; Chaoji went to Fenzhou and sent Jining circuit intendant Wang Changling and others with troops to suppress them, captured Benqing and others, and burned their stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhou garrison troops Li Benqing and Ren Zixing seized Tongzhu Stockade at Yongning. Chaoji went to Fenzhou, sent Jining intendant Wang Changling against them, captured the leaders, and burned the stockade.

sentences.zh: 寧鄉民楊春暢等復以左道據冷泉寨為亂，朝紀遣平陽副將范承宗等討平之，擢宣大山西總督。

translations.literal: Ningxiang commoners Yang Chunchang and others again used heterodox teachings to hold Lengquan Stockade in rebellion; Chaoji sent Pingyang deputy commander Fan Chengzong and others to suppress and pacify them, and was promoted to Xuanda-Shanxi governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxiang's Yang Chunchang again raised a heterodox sect at Lengquan Stockade. Chaoji sent Pingyang deputy commander Fan Chengzong to crush them and was promoted to Xuanda-Shanxi governor-general.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 延慶，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Yanqing, a man of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing was of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 入關，官至江西巡撫。

translations.literal: After entering the pass, he rose to the office of Jiangxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he became governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 順治間，治山、陝著績效者，又有馬之先、劉弘遇。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi, others who achieved notable results governing Shaanxi and Shanxi included Ma Zhixian and Liu Hongyu.
translations.idiomatic: Other notable Shaanxi and Shanxi administrators of the Shunzhi era were Ma Zhixian and Liu Hongyu.

sentences.zh: 馬之先，漢軍鑲藍旗人，初籍金州衛。

translations.literal: Ma Zhixian, a man of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner, was originally registered in Jinzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhixian of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner was originally registered in Jinzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 順治初，以諸生授昌平知州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, as a licentiate he was appointed magistrate of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi the licentiate was made magistrate of Changping.

sentences.zh: 四遷至湖廣布政使。

translations.literal: After four promotions he reached Huguang provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Four promotions brought him to Huguang administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，授江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was appointed Jiangxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 土寇王才據終南山肆掠，之先遣游擊陳明順等自子午鎮進剿，才竄走，敗之高關峪，又敗之化羊峪，獲才。

translations.literal: The bandit Wang Cai held Zhongnan Mountain and plundered widely; Zhixian sent battalion commander Chen Mingshun and others from Ziwu Town to suppress him; Cai fled, was defeated at Gaoguanyu, defeated again at Huayangyu, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Wang Cai raided from Zhongnan Mountain. Zhixian sent Chen Mingshun from Ziwu Town in pursuit, routed him at Gaoguanyu and Huayangyu, and captured him.

sentences.zh: 又捕治諸盜何紫山、孫守金、唐珍玉等。

translations.literal: He also captured and punished the bandits He Zishan, Sun Shoujin, Tang Zhenyu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also rounded up bandits He Zishan, Sun Shoujin, Tang Zhenyu, and others.

sentences.zh: 十一年，自成餘黨劉二虎、郝搖旗等侵入陝西境，之先與漢興總兵趙光興發兵三道迎擊，破小廣峪寨，斬其將傅奇，遷宣大山西總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Li Zicheng's remnant Liu Erhu, Hao Yaoqi, and others invaded Shaanxi; Zhixian with Hanxing regional commander Zhao Guangxing sent troops in three columns to meet them, broke Xiaoguangyu Stockade, beheaded their general Fu Qi, and he was transferred to Xuanda-Shanxi governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Liu Erhu and Hao Yaoqi invaded Shaanxi. Zhixian and Zhao Guangxing met them in three columns, stormed Xiaoguangyu Stockade, killed their general Fu Qi, and Zhixian was made Xuanda-Shanxi governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十三年，調川陝總督，加兵部尚書，入覲，上諭之曰：「陝西天下嚥喉，爾當視孟喬芳倍加勤慎，方克有濟。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred to Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, given the additional title of Minister of War, and on audience the emperor instructed him: "Shaanxi is the throat of the empire; you must be doubly diligent and careful beyond Meng Qiaofang if you are to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general and Minister of War. At audience the emperor told him: "Shaanxi is the empire's throat. You must be twice as diligent as Meng Qiaofang if you are to succeed."

sentences.zh: 」十四年，卒，諡勤僖。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he died; his posthumous title was Qinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year with the posthumous name Qinxi (Diligent and Joyful).

sentences.zh: 劉弘遇，漢軍正藍旗人，初籍遼東。

translations.literal: Liu Hongyu, a man of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongyu of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner was originally registered in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 與弟奇遇，並以諸生入祖大壽幕，佐軍諮。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Qiyu, both entered Zu Dashou's staff as licentiates to assist in military counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Qiyu, both licentiates, joined Zu Dashou's staff as military advisers.

sentences.zh: 天命間，太祖伐明，次三岔河，弘遇與奇遇挈家來歸，籍明諸邊兵馬數目，並畫戰守事陳奏。

translations.literal: During Tianming, when the Taizu campaigned against the Ming and halted at Sancha River, Hongyu and Qiyu brought their families to submit, recorded the numbers of Ming border troops and horses, and presented plans for attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianming, as the Taizu campaigned against the Ming at Sancha River, Hongyu and Qiyu submitted with their families, tallied Ming border forces, and presented attack and defense plans.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「得廣寧，當官汝！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When Guangning is taken, you shall be given office!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When we take Guangning, I will give you office!"

sentences.zh: 」久之未用。

translations.literal: For a long time he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: For a long time he went unused.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，上疏乞自效，命大學士範文程等試之，授弘文院副理事官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, he memorialized offering his service; Grand Secretaries Fan Wencheng and others were ordered to test him, and he was appointed associate director of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he offered his service, passed tests by Fan Wencheng and others, and became associate director of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，譯遼、金、元三史成，賜白金、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the translation of the Liao, Jin, and Yuan histories was completed, and he was granted silver and a saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 the Liao, Jin, and Yuan histories were completed in translation, and he received silver, a saddle, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 尋授工部理事官，遷山西朔州道。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed director in the Ministry of Works and transferred to Shuozhou circuit in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a Works Ministry director and was moved to Shuozhou circuit in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二年，與副將侯大節等捕治蔣家峪、黑草嘴土寇，擢陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the second year, with deputy commander Hou Dajie and others he suppressed bandits at Jiangjiayu and Heicaozui and was promoted to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he and deputy commander Hou Dajie suppressed bandits at Jiangjiayu and Heicaozui and was promoted to Shaanxi administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Anhui provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛江西，皖北盜蜂起。

translations.literal: When Jin Shengwan rebelled in Jiangxi, bandits swarmed in northern Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shengwan rebelled in Jiangxi, bandits flared across northern Anhui.

sentences.zh: 弘遇如池州，分遣鎮將逐捕盜渠王貳甫等，移駐安慶，與總督馬國柱捕治英山、霍山、潛山諸盜，得其渠孔文燦等，餘盜悉平。

translations.literal: Hongyu went to Chizhou, separately sent garrison commanders to hunt the bandit chief Wang Erfu and others, moved his headquarters to Anqing, and with Governor-General Ma Guozhu suppressed bandits in Yingshan, Huoshan, Qianshan, and other places, captured their chief Kong Wencan and others, and the remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyu went to Chizhou, sent commanders after Wang Erfu, moved to Anqing, and with governor-general Ma Guozhu cleared bandits in Yingshan, Huoshan, and Qianshan, taking chief Kong Wencan until the rest were pacified.

sentences.zh: 六年，裁缺召還。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, his post was abolished and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his post was cut and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 七年，授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was appointed Shanxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 時姜瓖亂初定，其黨竄匿保德、五台、府谷諸縣山谷間。

translations.literal: At that time Jiang Xiang's rebellion had just been pacified, and his followers hid in the mountain valleys of Baode, Wutai, Fugu, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiang's rebellion had just ended, and his followers hid in the mountains of Baode, Wutai, Fugu, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 弘遇請免逋賦，甦驛困，矜卹諸死事家。

translations.literal: Hongyu requested remission of arrears in tax, relief for courier stations in distress, and compassionate grants to families of those who died in service.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyu sought tax remissions, relief for exhausted courier stations, and pensions for families of the dead.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「兵後民田荒蕪殆盡，前此師討姜瓖，竭蹶供芻糧。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "After the war the people's fields are largely wasteland; earlier armies campaigning against Jiang Xiang exhausted themselves supplying fodder.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "After the war the fields lie largely fallow; earlier campaigns against Jiang Xiang had exhausted the people supplying fodder."

sentences.zh: 今捕治餘寇，日需輸輓。

translations.literal: Now in suppressing the remaining bandits, transport is needed daily.
translations.idiomatic: Now suppressing remnant bandits requires daily transport.

sentences.zh: 值二麥未收，秋禾遇蝗災，農失耕時。

translations.literal: It happens that the second wheat crop is not yet in, the autumn grain has suffered locust disaster, and farmers have missed the season for plowing.
translations.idiomatic: The second wheat crop is not in, autumn grain has been hit by locusts, and farmers have missed the plowing season.

sentences.zh: 」得旨，下所司蠲賑。

translations.literal: An edict was received, and the responsible offices were ordered to remit taxes and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the relevant offices to remit taxes and provide relief.

sentences.zh: 又與總督佟養量、總兵剛阿泰剿五台山寇劉永忠、高鼎，降陝西土寇楊茂。

translations.literal: Again with Governor-General Tong Yangliang and regional commander Gangatai he suppressed the Wutai Mountain bandits Liu Yongzhong and Gao Ding, and induced the Shaanxi bandit Yang Mao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With governor-general Tong Yangliang and regional commander Gangatai he suppressed Wutai bandits Liu Yongzhong and Gao Ding and induced Shaanxi bandit Yang Mao to surrender.

sentences.zh: 弘遇撫山西四年，建忠烈祠祀守土諸臣死姜瓖亂者，並修太原、陽曲學宮，築汾河諸堤，山西民誦其惠。

translations.literal: Hongyu governed Shanxi for four years, built a shrine to loyal martyrs honoring officials who died in Jiang Xiang's rebellion, and also repaired the school temples of Taiyuan and Yangqu and built dikes along the Fen River; the people of Shanxi praised his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In four years as Shanxi governor he built a martyrs' shrine for officials killed in Jiang Xiang's revolt, restored Taiyuan and Yangqu school temples, and built Fen River dikes; Shanxi people praised his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 旋以捕治土寇未入奏即籍沒，給事中張璿論弘遇專擅，尋奉詔甄別督撫，弘遇左授福建督糧道。

translations.literal: Soon because in suppressing bandits he had confiscated property before memorializing, Censor Zhang Xuan impeached Hongyu for acting on his own authority; soon an edict came to evaluate governors, and Hongyu was demoted to Fujian grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then impeached by censor Zhang Xuan for confiscating bandit property before reporting it. In a general review of governors he was demoted to Fujian grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year.

sentences.zh: 於時躍，漢軍正白旗人，初籍廣寧。

translations.literal: Yu Shiyue, a man of the Han Army Bordered White Banner, was originally registered in Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiyue of the Han Army Bordered White Banner was originally registered in Guangning.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，以諸生授安徽合肥知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, as a licentiate he was appointed magistrate of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 the licentiate was made magistrate of Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 尋遷河南懷慶知府。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Huaiqing prefect in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Huaiqing in Henan.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢河南道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to Henan circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Henan circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 靈寶、盧氏二縣寇發，時躍與副將寇徽音、游擊孔國養等入山捕治，破其寨，斬寇渠劉芳、張進澤、張三桂等，寇乃平。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Lingbao and Lushi counties, Shiyue with deputy commander Kou Huiyin, battalion commander Kong Guoyang, and others entered the mountains to suppress them, broke their stockades, and beheaded the bandit chiefs Liu Fang, Zhang Jinze, Zhang Sangui, and others, and the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Lingbao and Lushi, Shiyue with Kou Huiyin and Kong Guoyang stormed their mountain camps and executed chiefs Liu Fang, Zhang Jinze, and Zhang Sangui until the region was quiet.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷山西按察使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to Shanxi provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Shanxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時躍善聽訟，訟至即定讞，民稱之曰於不落。

translations.literal: Shiyue was skilled at hearing lawsuits; when a suit came he immediately decided the verdict, and the people called him "Yu Never Fails".
translations.idiomatic: Shiyue was famed for swift judgments; the people nicknamed him "Yu Never Fails" because cases left his court decided on the spot.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to Shanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Shanxi administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 坐在陝西薦舉屬吏失當，左遷。

translations.literal: For improperly recommending subordinates while in Shaanxi, he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted for faulty recommendations of subordinates while in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 經略洪承疇薦其才，命赴軍前效用。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou recommended his talent, and he was ordered to go to the army front to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou recommended him, and he was ordered to the front.

sentences.zh: 尋复薦補湖廣驛鹽道。

translations.literal: Soon he was again recommended and appointed to Huguang courier and salt circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed to Huguang courier and salt intendant.

sentences.zh: 十二年，超擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was promoted by special selection to Guangxi provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was exceptionally promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明宗人盛濃、盛添據富川，結土寇王心、蔣乾相等，勼集瑤、僮，窺旁近郡縣。

translations.literal: Ming clansmen Sheng Nong and Sheng Tian held Fuchuan, joined with bandits Wang Xin and Jiang Ganxiang and others, gathered Yao and Zhuang, and watched the neighboring prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Ming kinsmen Sheng Nong and Sheng Tian held Fuchuan, allied with bandits Wang Xin and Jiang Ganxiang, rallied Yao and Zhuang tribes, and menaced neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時躍會提督線國安、總兵全節討平之。

translations.literal: Shiyue joined with Grand Coordinator Xian Guo'an and regional commander Quan Jie to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyue joined grand coordinator Xian Guo'an and regional commander Quan Jie to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 十三年，明將龍韜屯柳州，時躍密約國安與定南王護衛李茹春、總兵溫如珍等，督兵攻之，陣斬韜，逐北三十餘裡，餘眾悉遁。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Ming general Long Tao encamped at Liuzhou; Shiyue secretly arranged with Guo'an and Prince of Dingnan's guard Li Ruchun, regional commander Wen Ruzhen, and others to direct troops against him, killed Tao in battle, pursued north more than thirty li, and the remainder all fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Ming general Long Tao held Liuzhou. Shiyue coordinated with Guo'an, Li Ruchun, and Wen Ruzhen, killed Tao in battle, pursued him thirty li, and routed his force.

sentences.zh: 十四年，師下雲南，時躍疏請賓州設兵防守，並分屯柳州備策應，下所司議行。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as the army descended on Yunnan, Shiyue memorialized requesting troops garrisoned at Binzhou for defense and detachments stationed at Liuzhou as reserve, and the responsible offices were ordered to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, as troops advanced on Yunnan, he asked for garrisons at Binzhou and Liuzhou; the ministries approved.

sentences.zh: 明桂王由榔號召諸降附土寇，假以公侯，分據郡縣：鬱林則李勝、李喬華，懷集則何奎豹、李盛功，富川、賀縣則馬寶、梁忠，南寧、太平則賀凡儀、曹友，並倚險為巢，四出侵掠。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui Zhu Youlang summoned the surrendered bandits, gave them false titles of duke and marquis, and divided the prefectures and counties among them: Yulin had Li Sheng and Li Qiaohua, Huaiji had He Kuibao and Li Shengong, Fuchuan and Hexian had Ma Bao and Liang Zhong, Nanning and Taiping had He Fanyi and Cao You—all held difficult terrain as lairs and raided on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui Zhu Youlang rallied surrendered bandits with bogus noble titles: Li Sheng and Li Qiaohua in Yulin, He Kuibao and Li Shengong in Huaiji, Ma Bao and Liang Zhong in Fuchuan and Hexian, He Fanyi and Cao You in Nanning and Taiping—all raided from mountain strongholds.

sentences.zh: 僮寇羅法達、廖仁倫等復擾臨桂、永福、荔浦、修仁諸縣。

translations.literal: Zhuang bandits Luo Fada, Liao Renlun, and others again harassed the counties of Lingui, Yongfu, Lipu, and Xiuren.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang bandits Luo Fada and Liao Renlun again harassed Lingui, Yongfu, Lipu, and Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 時躍親督兵捕治，所陷城邑次第克復，敘加都察院副都​​御史。

translations.literal: Shiyue personally directed troops to suppress them; the cities they had taken were recovered in succession, and he was given the additional title of Vice Censor-in-chief of the Left in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyue led the suppression in person; lost cities were recovered one by one, and he was made vice censor-in-chief of the left.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢廣西總督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was promoted to Guangxi governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he became governor-general of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明德陽王至濬走安南，時躍招使來降。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Yang of the Mingde era, Zhu Zhijun, fled to Annam; Shiyue induced him to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Yang Zhu Zhijun fled to Annam; Shiyue induced his surrender.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加右都御史。

translations.literal: Merit was reviewed: he was given the additional title of Censor-in-chief of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made censor-in-chief of the right.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 2.

sentences.zh: 蘇弘祖，漢軍正紅旗人，初籍遼陽。

translations.literal: Su Hongzu, a man of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner, was originally registered in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Su Hongzu of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner was originally registered in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，以舉人授戶部啟心郎，賜朝衣一襲，免丁四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde, as a provincial graduate he was appointed a censorial secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and granted one court robe and exemption from four corvée households.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 the provincial graduate became a Revenue Ministry censorial secretary and received a court robe and corvée exemptions.

sentences.zh: 八年，考滿，授世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, at the completion of his performance review, he was granted the hereditary rank of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his review earned him the hereditary rank of niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授河南河北道。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, he was appointed Henan north-of-the-Yellow River circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he became Henan north-of-the-Yellow River intendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷陝西布政使，世職累進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner, and his hereditary rank was advanced step by step to third-class Adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Shaanxi administration commissioner, and his line advanced to third-class Adahafan.

sentences.zh: 十年，坐計典失實，左授福建福寧道。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, for inaccuracies in the civil service examination records, he was demoted to Fujian Funing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was demoted to Funing circuit in Fujian for errors in examination records.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授南贛巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed Nan'gan provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became governor of southern Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，雩都寇發，弘祖斥資造火器，遣兵搗其巢，擒其渠李玉廷。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, bandits rose in Yudu; Hongzu spent his own funds to make firearms, sent troops to storm their lair, and captured their chief Li Yuting.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yudu bandits rose. Hongzu funded firearms, stormed their lair, and captured chief Li Yuting.

sentences.zh: 別有土寇謝上逵、羅一鑑、徐黃毛等，據廣東平遠五指石，界連閩、贛。

translations.literal: Separately, the bandits Xie Shangkui, Luo Yijian, Xu Huangmao, and others held Wuzhishi at Pingyuan in Guangdong, on the border with Fujian and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Other bandits Xie Shangkui, Luo Yijian, and Xu Huangmao held Wuzhishi in Guangdong's Pingyuan on the Fujian-Jiangxi border.

sentences.zh: 弘祖發兵討之，上逵詐降，潛走匿紅畬。

translations.literal: Hongzu sent troops to attack them; Shangkui feigned surrender and secretly fled to hide among the Red She.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzu attacked them; Shangkui feigned surrender and hid among the Red She people.

sentences.zh: 弘祖遣將李宗韜以計擒斬一鑑、黃毛等七人，夜進兵，逐賊至柑子窩中木溪，毀五指石寨，攻紅畬，賊縛上逵獻，斬之。

translations.literal: Hongzu sent the commander Li Zongtao to capture and behead Yijian, Huangmao, and seven others by stratagem; troops advanced by night, pursued the bandits to Ganziwo at Zhongmuxi, destroyed Wuzhishi Stockade, attacked the Red She, and the bandits bound Shangkui and presented him and he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongtao trapped and killed Yijian, Huangmao, and seven others. Night columns destroyed Wuzhishi Stockade, broke the Red She, and the rebels delivered Shangkui for execution.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遣游擊王把什捕治廣昌土寇，乘雨攻不備，破滴水、羊石二寨，斬千餘級，擒其渠幸連升、蕭來信。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he sent battalion commander Wang Bash to suppress Guangchang bandits; taking advantage of rain they attacked unprepared, broke Dingshui and Yangshi stockades, beheaded more than a thousand, and captured the chiefs Xing Liansheng and Xiao Laixin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Wang Bash stormed Guangchang bandits in the rain, took Dingshui and Yangshi stockades, killed over a thousand, and captured chiefs Xing Liansheng and Xiao Laixin.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，甄別督撫，弘祖解任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, in the evaluation of governors, Hongzu was relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 the governor review relieved him of office.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 吳景道，漢軍正黃旗人，初籍遼東廣寧衛。

translations.literal: Wu Jingdao, a man of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong Guangning Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jingdao of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner was originally registered in Guangning Guard, Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，授吏部啟心郎。

translations.literal: During Tiancong, he was appointed a censorial secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancong he became a Personnel Ministry censorial secretary.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，改都察院理事官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, he was reassigned as director of the Censorate.
