translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he became a Censorate director.

sentences.zh: 疏劾刑部理事官郎位貪污不法狀，鞫實，黜郎位，追贓貸死。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching the Justice Ministry director Lang Wei for corruption and lawlessness; investigation proved true, Wei was dismissed, his illicit gains were pursued, and he was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Justice Ministry director Lang Wei for corruption; the case was proved, Wei was dismissed, his gains were recovered, and he was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 郎位銜景道甚，誘都察院筆帖式李民表與同居，訐景道，鞫虛，民表坐誅，籍郎位半產。

translations.literal: Wei bore a deep grudge against Jingdao, induced Censorate clerk Li Minbiao to live with him, and denounced Jingdao; investigation proved false, Minbiao was executed, and half of Wei's property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei hated Jingdao, induced clerk Li Minbiao to denounce him, but the charge failed; Minbiao was executed and half of Wei's estate was seized.

sentences.zh: 景道以不察民表違禁移居他旗，罰如例。

translations.literal: Jingdao was fined as usual for failing to detect Minbiao's forbidden move to another Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdao was fined for not detecting Minbiao's illegal move to another Banner.

sentences.zh: 景道疏論睿親王多爾袞專擅，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Jingdao memorialized criticizing Prince Rui Dorgon for acting on his own authority and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against Prince Rui Dorgon's usurpation of authority and lost his post.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，起授河南布政使，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he was reappointed Henan provincial administration commissioner and promoted to provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he was restored as Henan administration commissioner and made governor.

sentences.zh: 時河北初定，河南五府餘寇未靖。

translations.literal: At that time Hebei had just been pacified, but remnant bandits in the five prefectures of Henan were not yet quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei was newly pacified, but bandits still troubled Henan's five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 寶豐宋養氣、新野陳蛟、商城黃景運等各聚數千人，侵掠城邑。

translations.literal: Song Yangqi of Baofeng, Chen Jiao of Xinye, Huang Jingyun of Shangcheng, and others each gathered several thousand men and raided cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yangqi of Baofeng, Chen Jiao of Xinye, and Huang Jingyun of Shangcheng each mustered thousands and raided towns.

sentences.zh: 景道檄總兵高第、副將沈朝華等分道捕治，誅養氣等。

translations.literal: Jingdao ordered regional commander Gao Di and deputy commander Shen Chaohua and others to suppress them by separate routes and executed Yangqi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdao sent Gao Di and Shen Chaohua in separate columns to suppress them and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 四年，鄖陽土寇王光泰率千餘人犯淅川，景道遣參將尤見等與總兵張應祥合兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Xunyang bandit Wang Guangtai led more than a thousand men to invade Xichuan; Jingdao sent brigade commander You Jian and others to join regional commander Zhang Yingxiang and repel them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Guangtai of Xunyang invaded Xichuan with over a thousand men; Jingdao and Zhang Yingxiang drove him off.

sentences.zh: 五年，羅山土寇張其倫據雞籠山寨，出掠，景道遣都司硃國強、佟文煥等督兵討之，破寨，擒戮其倫，併其黨硃智明、趙虎山等。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Luoshan bandit Zhang Qilun held Jilong Mountain Stockade and raided outward; Jingdao sent Commander Zhu Guoqiang, Tong Wenhuan, and others to lead troops against him, broke the stockade, captured and executed Qilun, and together with his followers Zhu Zhiming, Zhao Hushan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Zhang Qilun held Jilong Mountain Stockade. Zhu Guoqiang and Tong Wenhuan stormed it, executed Qilun, and took Zhu Zhiming and Zhao Hushan.

sentences.zh: 曹縣土寇範慎行等煽寧陵、商丘、考城、虞城、儀封、蘭陽、祥符、封丘諸縣土寇，並起為盜，屯黃河北岸。

translations.literal: The Caoxian bandit Fan Shenxing and others incited bandits in the counties of Ningling, Shangqiu, Kaocheng, Yucheng, Yifeng, Lanyang, Xiangfu, and Fengqiu to rise together as robbers and encamp on the north bank of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shenxing of Caoxian stirred bandits across eight counties to rise and camp on the Yellow River's north bank.

sentences.zh: 景道檄第督兵討之，寇退保長垣，第以師從之，寇走蘭陽。

translations.literal: Jingdao ordered Di to lead troops against them; the bandits retreated to hold Changyuan, Di followed with his army, and the bandits fled to Lanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdao ordered Di against them; the bandits fell back to Changyuan, then fled to Lanyang under pursuit.

sentences.zh: 景道遣文煥督兵追擊，斬千餘級。

translations.literal: Jingdao sent Wenhuan to lead troops in pursuit and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan pursued and killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 薄曹縣，寇列柵拒守。

translations.literal: Approaching Caoxian, the bandits set palisades to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Near Caoxian the bandits palisaded their camp.

sentences.zh: 景道檄總兵孔希貴自衛輝道肥城，斷寇東走路。

translations.literal: Jingdao ordered regional commander Kong Xigui to come from Weihui via Feicheng and cut off the bandits' eastern escape route.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdao sent Kong Xigui from Weihui through Feicheng to block their eastern escape.

sentences.zh: 游擊趙世泰、都司韓進等率精騎分道夾擊，戰於東明，殲寇數千，獲慎行誅之，餘眾悉潰散。

translations.literal: Battalion commander Zhao Shitai, Commander Han Jin, and others led picked cavalry in separate columns to strike together; fighting at Dongming, several thousand bandits were annihilated, Shenxing was captured and executed, and the remainder all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shitai and Han Jin struck from both flanks at Dongming, annihilated thousands, executed Shenxing, and scattered the rest.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Merit was reviewed: he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 七年，進尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became a full minister.

sentences.zh: 八年，商州土寇何紫山等掠盧氏，夜襲世泰營，第督兵扼擊，走商南。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Shangzhou bandit He Zishan and others plundered Lushi and raided Shitai's camp by night; Di directed troops to block and strike, and they fled to Shangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year He Zishan raided Lushi and night-attacked Shitai's camp; Di drove them to Shangnan.

sentences.zh: 景道檄應祥督兵討之，寇盡殲。

translations.literal: Jingdao ordered Yingxiang to lead troops against them, and the bandits were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdao sent Zhang Yingxiang to finish them off.

sentences.zh: 九年，以塞汴河決口，與河道總督楊方興同賜鞍馬、冠服。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for stopping the Yellow River breach at Bian, he and River Works Governor-General Yang Fangxing were together granted saddles, horses, caps, and robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he and river works governor-general Yang Fangxing received saddles, horses, and robes for sealing the Bian River breach.

sentences.zh: 十年，以老疾乞休。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, citing age and illness, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he retired on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，贈太子太保，諡愨僖。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he died; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Mixi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Mixi (Sincere and Joyful).

sentences.zh: 李日芃，漢軍正藍旗人，初籍遼陽。

translations.literal: Li Ripeng, a man of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner, was originally registered in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ripeng of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner was originally registered in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，命以諸生入內院理事，賜五戶。

translations.literal: During the Taizong's reign, he was ordered to enter the Inner Court as a licentiate to handle affairs and was granted five households.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taizong he entered the Inner Court as a licentiate and received five households.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授永平知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he became prefect of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷霸州兵備道。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Bazhou military preparedness commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Bazhou military preparedness commissioner.

sentences.zh: 授知州張儒策，諭降土寇李振宇等數百人，擢僉都御史。

translations.literal: He appointed Magistrate Zhang Ruce to induce several hundred bandits such as Li Zhenyu to surrender and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Through magistrate Zhang Ruce he induced hundreds of bandits led by Li Zhenyu to surrender and was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，加右副都御史，授操江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was given the additional title of Right Vice Censor-in-chief and appointed Caojiang provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became right vice censor-in-chief and Caojiang governor.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓以江西叛，日芃親督兵屯小孤山磨盤洲，令同知趙廷臣、參將汪義、游擊袁誠等迎擊。

translations.literal: When Jin Shengwan rebelled in Jiangxi, Ripeng personally directed troops encamped at Xiaogu Mountain Mopanzhou and ordered Vice Prefect Zhao Tingchen, brigade commander Wang Yi, battalion commander Yuan Cheng, and others to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Shengwan rebelled in Jiangxi, Ripeng encamped at Mopanzhou on Xiaogu Mountain and ordered Zhao Tingchen, Wang Yi, and Yuan Cheng to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 五年，戰於彭澤，得舟二十餘，寇中砲及溺死者無算。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, fighting at Pengze, more than twenty boats were taken; those struck by cannon and drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengze in the fifth year he captured more than twenty boats; cannon and drowning took a countless toll.

sentences.zh: 六年，裁安徽巡撫，命日芃攝其事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Anhui governorship was abolished and Ripeng was ordered to administer it in the interim.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the Anhui governorship was cut, Ripeng administered the province pro tempore.

sentences.zh: 土寇餘尚鑑挾明宗室統錡H0聲桓餘黨據險為二十餘寨，掠桐城、潛山、太湖諸縣。

translations.literal: The bandit Yu Shangjian, taking the Ming clansman Tong Qi and Shengwan's remnant followers, held difficult terrain in more than twenty stockades and raided Tongcheng, Qianshan, Taihu, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Yu Shangjian, backed by Ming clansman Tong Qi and Shengwan's remnants, held more than twenty mountain stockades and raided Tongcheng, Qianshan, and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 日芃遣副將梁大用等督兵討之，克皖澗寨，進圍飛旗寨，斷水道，分兵四路合擊，拔之。

translations.literal: Ripeng sent deputy commander Liang Dayong and others to lead troops against them, took Wan Stream Stockade, advanced to besiege Feiqi Stockade, cut the water route, divided forces in four columns to strike together, and stormed it.
translations.idiomatic: Ripeng sent Liang Dayong against them, took Wan Stream Stockade, besieged Feiqi Stockade, cut its water supply, and stormed it from four directions.

sentences.zh: 又破桃圍等寨，擒戮統錡、尚鑑，餘大小和山等十八寨皆降。

translations.literal: Again he broke Taowei and other stockades, captured and executed Tong Qi and Shangjian, and the remaining eighteen stockades large and small at Daheshan and elsewhere all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Taowei and other stockades, executed Tong Qi and Shangjian, and eighteen remaining stockades at Daheshan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 九年，加兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十年，討平徽州赤嶺土寇張惟良。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he suppressed and pacified the Chiling bandit Zhang Weiliang in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he suppressed Zhang Weiliang's Chiling bandits in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，甄別直省督撫，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, in the evaluation of provincial governors, he was given the additional title of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the governor review made him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明將張名振屢自海入江犯鎮江、瓜州，劫漕艘。

translations.literal: The Ming general Zhang Mingzhen repeatedly entered the Yangtze from the sea to attack Zhenjiang and Guazhou and seize grain transport boats.
translations.idiomatic: Ming general Zhang Mingzhen repeatedly raided from the sea into the Yangtze at Zhenjiang and Guazhou and seized grain transports.

sentences.zh: 日芃令於鎮江檀家洲測江水，淺則植椿，深則編筏，環以鐵索，阻來舟。

translations.literal: Ripeng ordered that at Tanjiazhou in Zhenjiang the Yangtze waters be measured; where shallow, piles were set, where deep, rafts were woven and ringed with iron chains to block incoming boats.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenjiang's Tanjiazhou he measured the river: piles where it was shallow, chained rafts where it was deep, to block enemy craft.

sentences.zh: 兩岸置砲，南自鎮江至圌山，北自瓜洲至三江口，建新堤，設木橋，通巡兵往來。

translations.literal: Cannon were placed on both banks; south from Zhenjiang to Mount Tu, north from Guazhou to Sanjiangkou, new dikes were built and wooden bridges set up for patrol troops to pass back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted guns on both banks from Zhenjiang to Mount Tu and Guazhou to Sanjiangkou, built dikes and bridges, and linked patrol routes.

sentences.zh: 令圌山、瓜洲等四營守備更番督水師防禦。

translations.literal: He ordered the four garrisons at Mount Tu, Guazhou, and elsewhere to rotate duty officers supervising the naval forces in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Four garrisons at Mount Tu and Guazhou rotated officers to command the naval defense.

sentences.zh: 五里置一汛，譏察詳密。

translations.literal: A post was set every five li with detailed inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Posts every five li provided tight surveillance.

sentences.zh: 諸寇匿江為藪，俘斬略盡。

translations.literal: Bandits hiding on the river as a lair were captured and beheaded nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: River bandits were hunted down almost to extinction.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 旋卒，諡忠敏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; his posthumous title was Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and received the posthumous name Zhongmin (Loyal and Alert).

sentences.zh: 劉清泰，漢軍正紅旗人，初籍遼陽，名朝卿，以諸生歸太宗，賜今名。

translations.literal: Liu Qingtai, a man of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner, was originally registered in Liaoyang; his name was Chaoqing; as a licentiate he submitted to the Taizong and was granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qingtai of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner was born Chaoqing in Liaoyang; as a licentiate he submitted to the Taizong and received his present name.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年，試一等，入內院辦事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongde, he tested first class, entered the Inner Court to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 6 he ranked first in examinations and entered the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，擢弘文院學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he was promoted to academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he became a Hongwen Institute academician.

sentences.zh: 九年，充會試副考官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he served as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was associate metropolitan examination examiner.

sentences.zh: 授浙江福建總督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Zhejiang-Fujian governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor-general of Zhejiang and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功據廈門，陷漳浦、海澄、南靖諸縣，上命其父芝龍作書，敕清泰諭降。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen and had taken Zhangpu, Haicheng, Nanjing, and other counties; the emperor ordered his father Zhilong to write a letter commanding Qingtai to induce surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen and had seized Zhangpu, Haicheng, and Nanjing. The emperor had his father Zhilong write ordering Qingtai to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，清泰疏劾巡撫張學聖、巡道黃澍、總兵馬得功前此偵成功赴粵，潛襲廈門，攫其家貲，致成功修怨，連陷城邑，學聖等並坐黜。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year, Qingtai memorialized impeaching Governor Zhang Xuesheng, circuit intendant Huang Shu, and regional commander Ma Degong for earlier spying on Chenggong's departure for Guangdong, secretly raiding Xiamen, and seizing his family property, causing Chenggong to nurse a grudge and take cities in succession; Xuesheng and the others were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year Qingtai impeached Zhang Xuesheng, Huang Shu, and Ma Degong for raiding Xiamen while Chenggong was in Guangdong and looting his household, provoking reprisals; all three were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三月，清泰得成功報芝龍書，略言就撫後，原得浙東、嶺南地駐兵。

translations.literal: In the third month, Qingtai received Chenggong's reply to Zhilong's letter, stating briefly that after accepting pacification he wished to station troops in eastern Zhejiang and southern Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Chenggong replied to Zhilong that after submission he wanted troops in eastern Zhejiang and southern Fujian.

sentences.zh: 清泰疏上聞，並論成功語浮誇，議撫當詳慎，上嘉其遠慮。

translations.literal: Qingtai memorialized reporting this, also arguing that Chenggong's words were boastful and that pacification should be handled with care; the emperor praised his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtai reported the reply, called Chenggong's terms extravagant, and urged caution; the emperor praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 五月，平南將軍金礪攻海澄，以餉不繼，還軍漳浦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Pacification General Jin Li attacked Haicheng; because supplies did not follow, the army returned to Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Pacification General Jin Li attacked Haicheng but withdrew to Zhangpu for lack of supplies.

sentences.zh: 會上敕封成功海澄公，畀以泉、漳、惠、潮四郡地，遂罷兵。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor ordered Chenggong enfeoffed as Duke of Haicheng and given the four prefectures Quan, Zhang, Hui, and Chao, and hostilities ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The court then enfeoffed Chenggong Duke of Haicheng with Quan, Zhang, Hui, and Chao, and fighting paused.

sentences.zh: 清泰請駐軍浦城備不虞，從之。

translations.literal: Qingtai requested troops garrisoned at Pucheng against the unexpected; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtai asked to garrison Pucheng against surprises, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏言：「成功雖降，不薙發，其黨逞掠如故，降無實意。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he memorialized: "Although Chenggong has submitted, he will not shave his head, and his followers raid as before; the submission has no sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he wrote: "Chenggong has submitted but refuses the queue and his men still raid—the surrender is not sincere."

sentences.zh: 宜發禁旅赴福建，駐要地，資策應。

translations.literal: Banner guards should be sent to Fujian, stationed at key points to support operations.
translations.idiomatic: He urged sending guards to Fujian's key points as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 」下諸王大臣議。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the princes and ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the princes and ministers for debate.

sentences.zh: 清泰旋以病乞假，還駐杭州。

translations.literal: Qingtai soon cited illness to request leave and returned to station at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtai soon took sick leave and returned to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 成功發兵攻陷漳、泉，上授鄭親王世子濟度為定遠大將軍，率師討之。

translations.literal: Chenggong sent troops to take Zhang and Quan; the emperor appointed Prince Zheng's heir Jidu as commander-in-chief of the distant expedition to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong seized Zhang and Quan; Prince Zheng's heir Jidu was made commander-in-chief to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 左都御史龔鼎孳疏劾清泰當金礪攻海澄，不能同心合力，及招撫未定，又不控扼險要，致海疆被陷，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-chief Gong Dingzi memorialized impeaching Qingtai for failing to cooperate when Jin Li attacked Haicheng, and for not holding strategic points while pacification was unsettled, causing the coast to fall; he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Left censor-in-chief Gong Dingzi impeached Qingtai for failing to cooperate with Jin Li at Haicheng and leaving the coast exposed during negotiations; he lost his post.

sentences.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，起秘書院學士，授河南總督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Sacred Ancestor took the throne, he was reappointed academician of the Secretariat and made Henan governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, at the Kangxi succession, he became Secretariat academician and Henan governor-general.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，以報墾荒地萬餘頃，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi, for reporting more than ten thousand qing of newly reclaimed wasteland, he was given the additional title of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he reported reclaiming more than ten thousand qing of wasteland and was made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，以疾致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired for illness in the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 佟岱，漢軍正藍旗人，先世居佟佳。

translations.literal: Tong Dai, a man of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner; his family originally dwelt at Tongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Dai of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner came from Tongjia.

sentences.zh: 父佟三，歸太祖，任梅勒額真。

translations.literal: His father Tong San submitted to the Taizu and served as meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong San submitted to the Taizu and became a meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 佟岱與兄養量同授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Tong Dai and his elder brother Yangliang were together appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Dai and his elder brother Yangliang were both appointed niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 養量順治初官至宣大總督，駐陽和，有惠於民。

translations.literal: Yangliang early in Shunzhi rose to Xuanda governor-general, stationed at Yanghe, and had kindness for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yangliang early in Shunzhi became Xuanda governor-general at Yanghe and was beloved by the people.

sentences.zh: 佟岱崇德元年從伐朝鮮，以縱掠降民坐死，命奪官，罰鍰以贖。

translations.literal: Tong Dai in the first year of Chongde followed the campaign against Korea; for plundering surrendered people he was sentenced to death, ordered stripped of office, and fined to redeem his life.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 Tong Dai joined the Korean campaign but was condemned to death for plundering surrendered people; the sentence was commuted to dismissal and a fine.

sentences.zh: 三年，授吏部副理事官，兼甲喇額真。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed associate director of the Personnel Ministry and concurrently jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became associate Personnel director and jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 六年，師圍錦州，七年，攻塔山、杏山，皆在行，擢正藍旗漢軍梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the army besieged Jinzhou; in the seventh year, in the attacks on Tashan and Xingshan, he was present throughout and was promoted to meiren ejen of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was present through the Jinzhou siege and the seventh-year attacks on Tashan and Xingshan, and was promoted to meiren ejen of the Bordered Blue Han Army.

sentences.zh: 八年，從克前屯衛、中後所，予世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, following the capture of Qiantunwei and Zhonghousuo, he was granted the hereditary rank of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the capture of Qiantunwei and Zhonghousuo and received the hereditary rank of niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從克太原。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he followed the capture of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he joined the capture of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 二年，從討李自成，師自陝西徇湖廣，遂下江南。

translations.literal: In the second year, he followed the campaign against Li Zicheng; the army marched from Shaanxi through Huguang and then descended on Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he campaigned against Li Zicheng from Shaanxi through Huguang into Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 與總兵金聲桓駐守九江，定南康、南昌、瑞州、袁州諸府，以所俘獲奏聞。

translations.literal: With regional commander Jin Shengwan he garrisoned Jiujiang, pacified Nankang, Nanchang, Ruizhou, Yuanzhou, and other prefectures, and reported the captives taken.
translations.idiomatic: With Jin Shengwan he garrisoned Jiujiang and pacified Nankang, Nanchang, Ruizhou, and Yuanzhou, reporting his captives.

sentences.zh: 因疏言：「故明鍾祥王慈若等衰殘廢棄，或存其餘喘，彰我朝浩蕩之仁。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized: "The former Ming Prince of Zhongxiang Cimin and others are broken in body and cast aside; if their remaining breath is preserved, it will display our dynasty's vast benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that broken Ming princes such as Cimin of Zhongxiang might be spared to show the dynasty's magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 」得旨：「故明諸王赴京朝見。

translations.literal: An edict was received: "Former Ming princes are to come to the capital for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered former Ming princes to appear at court.

sentences.zh: 」旋令攝湖廣總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to administer Huguang governor-general affairs in the interim.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting Huguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 三年，還京，授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year, he returned to the capital and was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned to Beijing as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 復從徵湖南，自岳州進長沙，戰衡州，克寶慶、武岡。

translations.literal: Again he followed the Hunan campaign, advancing from Yuezhou into Changsha, fighting at Hengzhou, and taking Baoqing and Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: He again campaigned in Hunan from Yuezhou through Changsha and Hengzhou to Baoqing and Wugang.

sentences.zh: 六年，復從討姜瓖，拔渾源、左衛、朔州、汾州、太谷諸城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he again followed the campaign against Jiang Xiang and took the cities of Hunyuan, Zuowei, Shuozhou, Fenzhou, and Taigu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the Jiang Xiang campaign and took Hunyuan, Zuowei, Shuozhou, Fenzhou, and Taigu.

sentences.zh: 世職累進一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番，歷戶、吏諸部。

translations.literal: His hereditary rank was advanced step by step to first-class Adahafan with an additional Tosahafan, and he served in the Revenue, Personnel, and other ministries.
translations.idiomatic: His line rose to first-class Adahafan with Tosahafan, and he served in Revenue, Personnel, and other ministries.

sentences.zh: 十一年，代清泰為浙江福建總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he replaced Qingtai as Zhejiang-Fujian governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he replaced Qingtai as Zhejiang-Fujian governor-general.

sentences.zh: 疏請申海禁，斷接濟，片帆不得出海，違者罪至死。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting enforcement of the sea ban, cutting off all aid, so that not a single sail might put to sea, with violators punished up to death.
translations.idiomatic: He urged strict maritime prohibition: no sail at sea, no aid to rebels, death for violators.

sentences.zh: 十二年，成功陷舟山，十三年，复陷台州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Chenggong took Zhoushan; in the thirteenth year, he took Taizhou again.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong took Zhoushan in the twelfth year and Taizhou again in the thirteenth.

sentences.zh: 佟岱與巡撫秦世禎不協，互劾。

translations.literal: Tong Dai and Governor Qin Shizhen were at odds and impeached each other.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Dai and governor Qin Shizhen clashed and impeached each other.

sentences.zh: 上為移世禎操江巡撫，召佟岱還京，以李率泰代。

translations.literal: The emperor moved Shizhen to Caojiang governor and recalled Tong Dai to the capital; Li Shuaitai replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor transferred Shizhen to Caojiang and recalled Tong Dai; Li Shuaitai replaced him.

sentences.zh: 佟岱不即行，复疏自敘剿撫功，上責其冒功戀祿，下李率泰等按狀，奪官，留軍功三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: Tong Dai did not depart at once but again memorialized recounting his suppression and pacification merit; the emperor rebuked him for claiming merit and clinging to salary, ordered Li Shuaitai and others to investigate, stripped him of office, and retained only his military merit rank of third-class Adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Dai delayed departure and claimed credit; the emperor rebuked his greed, investigated through Li Shuaitai, dismissed him, and left only third-class Adahafan for military merit.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 秦世禎，漢軍正藍旗人，初籍廣寧。

translations.literal: Qin Shizhen, a man of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner, was originally registered in Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shizhen of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner was originally registered in Guangning.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，以貢生除直隸文安知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, as a tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Wen'an in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 the tribute student became magistrate of Wen'an in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 三年，行取授御史，疏請畫一各省裁免賦役，從之。

translations.literal: In the third year, selected by special promotion he was appointed censor and memorialized requesting uniform cuts and exemptions of tax and labor levies in each province; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became a censor and won approval for uniform provincial tax and labor cuts.

sentences.zh: 四年，巡按浙江。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he inspected Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he inspected Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 八年，甄別台員，列一等。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, in the evaluation of censorial officials, he was ranked first class.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he ranked first class among censors.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡按江南。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to inspect Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to inspect Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 世禎察淮、揚各郡蠹役害民，嚴治其罪。

translations.literal: Shizhen investigated corrupt clerks harming the people in the Huai-Yang prefectures and punished them severely.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed corrupt clerks harming people in the Huai-Yang region and punished them harshly.

sentences.zh: 徒黨聚盟，仇訴告者，世禎執為首者係之獄，疏上其事，並言懲蠹於事後，不若使不為蠹。

translations.literal: When factions gathered in leagues and sued informers, Shizhen arrested the ringleaders and imprisoned them, memorialized reporting the matter, and also said that punishing corruption after the fact was inferior to preventing corruption from arising.
translations.idiomatic: When clerk factions sued informers, he jailed the ringleaders and argued prevention beat punishment after the fact.

sentences.zh: 請飭督撫以下至州縣，毋於經制外濫設胥役，並定年限，毋令久充，上從之。

translations.literal: He requested that governors and below down to counties not appoint clerks beyond the statutory establishment, and fix term limits so they did not serve long; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that officials not exceed statutory clerk quotas or keep clerks too long; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時方大兵後，田畝淆亂，官為丈量，胥役因緣為奸。

translations.literal: At that time, just after major warfare, field boundaries were confused and officials measured land, while clerks used the opportunity for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars, field boundaries were chaotic; official surveys let clerks commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 世禎令編列「魚鱗冊」，使民自丈量，贏縮胥復其舊，荒坍皆有別。

translations.literal: Shizhen ordered compilation of the "Fish-Scale Register," letting the people measure themselves; surplus and shortage returned to the old norms, and wasteland and collapse were separately distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced the Fish-Scale Register for self-measurement by households, restoring accurate acreage and distinguishing wasteland from collapse.

sentences.zh: 州縣徵賦，民或逾額輸納，世禎限夏稅五月，秋糧九月，先給「易知單」，示以科則定數。

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties collected taxes, the people sometimes paid beyond the quota; Shizhen limited summer tax to the fifth month and autumn grain to the ninth, first issuing an "Easy-Knowledge Slip" showing the fixed rates.
translations.idiomatic: To stop over-collection he fixed summer tax in the fifth month and autumn grain in the ninth, issuing Easy-Knowledge Slips with fixed rates.

sentences.zh: 又令每甲匯列賦額及輸戶為「滾單」，使里長按戶遞傳，輸賦則填注。

translations.literal: He also ordered each community head to compile the tax quota and paying households into a "Rolling Register," so the village head could pass it household by household and note payment when tax was delivered.
translations.idiomatic: He added Rolling Registers listing quotas and payers for village heads to circulate and mark payments.

sentences.zh: 先行之蘇州，民以為便，條列以聞，通行諸府。

translations.literal: First implemented in Suzhou, the people found it convenient; it was listed in a memorial and extended to all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Piloted in Suzhou, the system pleased taxpayers and was extended province-wide.

sentences.zh: 又以徵銀設櫃，有司奉行不實，請增司府印封，立日收簿，輸戶自封投櫃，驗數書之簿。

translations.literal: Again, because silver collection used counters but officials did not implement it faithfully, he requested added seals from the prefecture and circuit, a daily receipt book, sealed deposits by payers, and verification written in the book.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened tax counters with prefectural seals, daily receipt books, and sealed deposits by taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 又請革僉點糧長之例，改官收官兌。

translations.literal: He also requested abolishing the practice of appointing grain chiefs by lot and changing to official collection and official remittance.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished lottery-appointed grain chiefs in favor of official collection and remittance.

sentences.zh: 並下部，著為令。

translations.literal: All were sent to the ministries and established as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries enacted all of this as law.

sentences.zh: 巡撫土國寶貪酷病民，以世禎劾，罷。

translations.literal: Governor Tu Guobao was greedy and cruel and harmed the people; because Shizhen impeached him, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tu Guobao was dismissed after Shizhen impeached his cruelty and greed.

sentences.zh: 十年，還京，遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he returned to the capital and was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he returned to Beijing as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢浙江巡撫，疏請增造戰艦，精選水師；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was promoted to Zhejiang provincial governor and memorialized requesting additional construction of warships and careful selection of naval forces;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became Zhejiang governor and asked for more warships and better naval selection;

sentences.zh: 別疏言沿海漁舟，往往通寇，請按保甲法，以二十五舟為一隊，無事聽採捕，有事助守禦：並議行。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said that coastal fishing boats often communicated with bandits and requested application of the baojia system, with twenty-five boats as one unit: in peace they might fish, in emergency they would aid defense; this too was deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: he also urged baojia grouping of fishing boats—twenty-five per unit, fishing in peace and aiding defense in crisis—and the plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與佟岱互劾，調操江巡撫，解佟岱任，命暫管總督事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he and Tong Dai impeached each other; he was transferred to Caojiang governor, Tong Dai was relieved, and he was ordered temporarily to administer governor-general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he and Tong Dai traded impeachments; he became Caojiang governor, replaced Tong Dai temporarily as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 尋以李率泰等疏論成功陷舟山，世禎不能辭咎，與佟岱並奪官。

translations.literal: Soon, because Li Shuaitai and others memorialized that Chenggong had taken Zhoushan and Shizhen could not escape blame, both he and Tong Dai were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shuaitai blamed him for Chenggong's capture of Zhoushan, both he and Tong Dai lost their posts.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 陳錦，字天章，漢軍正藍旗人，初籍錦州。

translations.literal: Chen Jin, style Tianzhang, a man of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner, was originally registered in Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jin (style Tianzhang) of the Han Army Bordered Blue Banner was originally from Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕明官大凌河都司，崇德間來降，予世職牛錄章京，加半個前程。

translations.literal: He served the Ming as commander of Dalinghe Guard; he came over in the Chongde period and was granted the hereditary rank of niru janggin with half a qian-cheng advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He had been Ming commander at Dalinghe Guard and surrendered in the Chongde era, receiving niru janggin rank and half a qian-cheng advancement.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: When the Han Army Banners were established, he was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han Army Banners were organized he became niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，自內院副理事官授登萊巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, from associate director of the Inner Court he was appointed Deng-Lai provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he moved from Inner Court associate director to governor of Dengzhou and Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 青州土寇楊威、秦尚行結明將劉澤清為亂，錦遣兵討平之。

translations.literal: The Qingzhou bandits Yang Wei and Qin Shangxing joined the Ming general Liu Zeqing in rebellion; Jin sent troops to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou bandits Yang Wei and Qin Shangxing joined Ming general Liu Zeqing; Jin suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 二年，土寇張廣焚掠掖、濰諸縣，遣兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the second year, the bandit Zhang Guang burned and plundered Yi and Wei counties; troops were sent and he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zhang Guang raided Yi and Wei; Jin's troops defeated him.

sentences.zh: 廣降於澤清，复寇平度，犯萊州，錦遣兵捕治，授策設伏徐家甿，射殺廣，盡殲其眾。

translations.literal: Guang submitted to Zeqing and again raided Pingdu and attacked Laizhou; Jin sent troops to suppress him, set an ambush at Xujiameng by stratagem, shot and killed Guang, and annihilated his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Guang rejoined Zeqing, raided Pingdu and Laizhou; Jin ambushed him at Xujiameng, killed him, and destroyed his band.

sentences.zh: 擢操江總督，與招撫大學士洪承疇並駐江寧。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Caojiang governor-general and together with pacification Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou was stationed at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He became Caojiang governor-general and was stationed at Jiangning with Hong Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 三年，明瑞昌王誼石等密結城人為亂，錦與承疇诇知之，閉城捕治諸為亂者。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Ming Prince of Ruichang Yishi and others secretly joined with people in the city to rebel; Jin and Chengchou learned by espionage, closed the city, and arrested those who had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Ming Prince of Ruichang Yishi plotted within the city; Jin and Chengchou learned of it, sealed the gates, and arrested the conspirators.

sentences.zh: 誼石以兵至，擊破之。

translations.literal: Yishi came with troops; they were defeated and broken.
translations.idiomatic: Yishi marched in force and was routed.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「圌山為鎮江咽喉，江寧門戶，宜建立砲台，置兵備。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he memorialized: "Mount Tu is the throat of Zhenjiang and the gateway of Jiangning; cannon forts should be built and troops stationed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he argued that Mount Tu guarded Zhenjiang and Jiangning's approaches and needed forts and garrisons.

sentences.zh: 江北要口設台亦如之。

translations.literal: Key points on the north bank should have forts as well.
translations.idiomatic: The north bank needed the same.

sentences.zh: 兩岸兵船接哨分防，沿江設烽墩，使聲勢相通。

translations.literal: Patrol boats on both banks should link sentries and divide defense; beacon towers should be set along the river so signals connect.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol craft, divided defenses, and river beacons should link the line.

sentences.zh: 」章下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved and implemented the plan.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江福建總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang-Fujian governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Zhejiang-Fujian governor-general.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功為寇，據延平將軍寨，地高險，俯瞰諸縣，攻不能破。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong was a rebel and held the Yanping general's stockade on high, difficult ground overlooking the counties; attacks could not break it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong held the lofty, impregnable Yanping general's stockade overlooking the region.

sentences.zh: 錦命壘土高與寨等，乘以登陴，遂克之。

translations.literal: Jin ordered earth piled as high as the stockade to mount the walls, and it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jin built an earthen ramp as high as the stockade and stormed it.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，錦遣兵次第收復，撫輯流亡，民賴以安。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine, Jin sent troops to recover territory in succession, soothed and gathered the displaced, and the people relied on him for security.
translations.idiomatic: During famine he recovered territory in stages, resettled refugees, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 五年，成功將鄭彩以舟師入據長樂、連江諸縣，錦與靖南將軍陳泰等分兵收復。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Chenggong's general Zheng Cai entered with a fleet and occupied Changle, Lianjiang, and other counties; Jin with Pacification General Chen Tai and others divided forces to recover them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Zheng Cai seized Changle and Lianjiang by sea; Jin and Chen Tai recovered them in divided columns.

sentences.zh: 師進次興化，斬成功將顧世臣等十一人。

translations.literal: The army advanced to Xinghua and beheaded Chenggong's generals Gu Shichen and eleven others.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinghua they beheaded eleven of Chenggong's generals including Gu Shichen.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣總兵張應夢、馬得功等復羅源、永春、德化、福安諸城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he sent regional commanders Zhang Yingmeng, Ma Degong, and others to recover Luoyuan, Yongchun, Dehua, Fu'an, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhang Yingmeng and Ma Degong recovered Luoyuan, Yongchun, Dehua, Fu'an, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 江西山寇侵延平，陷大田、尤溪，錦遣兵收復，獲明新建王由模等。

translations.literal: Jiangxi mountain bandits invaded Yanping and took Datian and Youxi; Jin sent troops to recover them and captured the Ming Prince of Xinjian Zhu Youmo and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi mountain bandits took Datian and Youxi in Yanping; Jin recovered them and captured the Ming Prince of Xinjian Zhu Youmo.

sentences.zh: 七年，疏請進攻舟山。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he memorialized requesting an advance against Zhoushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he asked to attack Zhoushan.

sentences.zh: 八年，錦與固山額真金礪、劉之源，提督田雄等會師，以大艦隨潮出，敗明兵於橫洋，獲其將阮進；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Jin with gushan ejen Jin Li, Liu Zhiyuan, Grand Coordinator Tian Xiong, and others united their armies; great ships followed the tide out and defeated Ming troops at Hengyang, capturing their general Ruan Jin;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jin, Jin Li, Liu Zhiyuan, and Tian Xiong combined fleets, defeated Ming forces at Hengyang on the tide, and captured Ruan Jin;

sentences.zh: 乘霧攻舟山，明魯王以海出走，遂克之，隳其城，置定關總兵，駐師守焉。

translations.literal: taking advantage of fog they attacked Zhoushan; the Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai fled, and it was taken; the city was demolished, a Dingguan regional commander was established, and troops were stationed to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: they took Zhoushan in fog, drove out the Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Yihai, razed the city, and garrisoned it under a Dingguan commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，成功寇漳浦、平和，錦督兵赴援，戰江東橋，敗績，左次同安，賊夜入其帳，刺中要害，遂卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Chenggong raided Zhangpu and Pinghe; Jin led troops to relieve them, fought at Jiangdong Bridge, was defeated, halted at Tong'an, and the bandits entered his tent by night, stabbed him in a vital place, and he died; he was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Chenggong raided Zhangpu and Pinghe. Jin was beaten at Jiangdong Bridge, fell back to Tong'an, and was stabbed in his tent at night; he died and was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國初民志未壹，諸依山海險岨而起者，往往自託於明遺，要之為民害，廓清摧陷，封疆之責也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the beginning of the dynasty the people's will was not yet unified; those who rose relying on mountain and sea defiles often claimed allegiance to Ming remnants, but in the end they harmed the people, and to clear and overthrow them was the duty of those who guarded the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator notes that early in the dynasty many rebels used mountains and coasts while claiming Ming loyalty, yet they harmed the people; clearing them was a frontier commander's duty.

sentences.zh: 國英定四川，合師討茅麓山，績最高。

translations.literal: Guoying pacified Sichuan and joined armies to suppress Maolu Mountain; his achievement was the highest.
translations.idiomatic: Guoying's pacification of Sichuan and the Maolu Mountain campaign rank highest.

sentences.zh: 武元守贛州，庫禮守淮安，全才守漢中，禦寇全城，亦其亞也。

translations.literal: Wuyuan held Ganzhou, Ku Li held Huai'an, and Quancai held Hanzhong, defending their cities against invaders; they rank next.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan at Ganzhou, Ku Li at Huai'an, and Quancai at Hanzhong—each held a city through siege—come next.

sentences.zh: 朝紀等捕治土寇，皆能勤其官者。

translations.literal: Chaoji and the others in suppressing local bandits were all able to be diligent in their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoji and others who suppressed local bandits likewise served diligently.

sentences.zh: 若清泰策鄭成功，謂挾怨而叛，殊不中事理。

translations.literal: As for Qingtai's policy toward Zheng Chenggong, saying he rebelled out of resentment, that truly missed the logic of events.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtai's claim that Chenggong rebelled from personal resentment, however, misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 錦屢勝而挫，遽為何人所賊，防衛亦稍疏矣。

translations.literal: Jin won repeatedly yet suffered setbacks and was suddenly slain by someone—his precautions were somewhat lax as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jin won often yet died suddenly in defeat; his guard was somewhat lax.
